articles.summary: Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer to stand down as an MP triggering a by-election.
articles.body: Today, after standing down as Prime Minister earlier this summer, Keir Starmer has decided to announce his resignation as MP for Holborn and St Pancras. It comes on Andy Burnham’s first day addressing MPs in the House of Commons as Prime Minister. Was the timing deliberate, or coincidental? Prime Minister Burnham has returned to the House of Commons after Summer Recess promising to 'unlock a feeling of positivity and possibility' - but what issues are awaiting the new-ish prime minister? articles.title: Best Weighted Blankets of 2026: 5 Expert-Recommended Options
articles.summary: Find the best weighted blankets for you and learn how to shop for the right one. Browse highly rated weighted blankets from Amazon, Baloo Living, Gravity Blanket and more.
articles.body: Weighted blankets have seen a lot of mainstream success within the last decade, but they’ve been around for much longer: Occupational therapists began studying the effects of weighted blankets and weighted vests in the early 2000s, and studies looking at the therapeutic effects of weighted blankets date even earlier. Studies show that weighted blankets — which are typically filled with small glass or plastic beads to add weight — can help you sleep better, reduce anxiety and relieve stress. Although our experts say a weighted blanket’s efficacy varies from person to person, it can provide positive effects both physically and psychologically. I consulted with sleep medicine specialists and occupational therapy experts about the potential benefits of weighted blankets, along with who should (and shouldn’t) use them. I also compiled a list of product recommendations that align with their guidance. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Highly-rated weighted blankets Our experts say a weighted blanket should provide multiple weight options to fit the 10% body weight limit, feature a machine-washable and breathable cover and offer a return policy that lets you trial the blanket before committing to it. With this guidance in mind, I rounded up highly rated weighted blankets, including a few NBC Selected staff favorites. Baloo Living’s weighted blanket features glass beads and comes in various sizes, ranging from 12 to 25 pounds. I own the 12-pound throw blanket, which fits snugly on my couch and offers a comfortable weight when I’m relaxing in the evening. The blanket is made with a 100% cotton exterior and interior, and it’s both machine-washable and dryer-safe, according to the brand (although it recommends using a commercial washing machine for the largest, 25-pound blanket). The blanket also features small loops sewn into the seams at the sides and corners to connect to a duvet cover, and it’s available in multiple colors. The Gravity Blanket features a machine-washable micro-plush duvet cover and an inner weighted piece filled with glass beads that can be hand-washed only. The inner weighted blanket also has gridded stitching to ensure the beads are uniformly distributed and don’t shift as you move around, according to the brand. For a kid-friendly option, this 5-pound weighted blanket from Harkla comes with an inner weighted layer and a removable fleece duvet cover that the brand says can be machine-washed in cold water and put in the dryer at a low setting. Harkla also offers a 7-pound, 10-pound and 15-pound version of the blanket for older kids and adults, and it comes in three colors. This YNM Weighted Blanket is another option that is both machine-washable and dryer-safe, but it recommends washing the duvet cover rather than the inner blanket, since frequent washing can cause wear and tear. It’s offered in a range of colorways and weights. We love cuddling up with Bearaby’s weighted animals and the brand’s weighted blankets are just as cozy. This one is 100 percent organic cotton and in a chunky knit pattern that looks and feels luxe. It also comes with a dust bag so you can store it properly or take it on your travels. How to shop for a weighted blanket Two of our experts — Dr. Seema Khosla, medical director of the North Dakota Center for Sleep, and Michael Urban, occupational therapy practitioner, senior lecturer and director of the Doctorate of Occupational Therapy Program at the University of New Haven — say trialing a weighted blanket before making a final decision is typically a good call, especially since many weighted blanket brands offer a 30-day return policy. Here are some additional features to consider: What is the best weight for a weighted blanket? While 10% of your body weight is recommended, it’s ultimately based on personal preference and you should ensure that “movement and breathing are not impaired,” says Dr. Alex Dimitriu, board-certified psychiatrist and sleep medicine specialist at SiliconPsych. Khosla also recommends starting with a low weight — around 5 pounds or less — to see how it feels. “Don’t invest a lot of money in your first one, and just try it if you’re taking a nap or relaxing in the evening while reading or watching TV — if you love it, you can always upgrade to a better one for the bedroom,” she says. How important is breathability? Since the pressure created by a weighted blanket can make it feel warmer than a typical blanket, Dimitriu recommends looking for one that features a cover made from a breathable fabric — like cotton or linen — to help your body cool off at night and facilitate deep and restorative sleep. The quicker our core body temperature drops, the quicker we can fall asleep, so overheating at night can disrupt your overall sleep quality, Khosla adds. What is the best type of cover for a weighted blanket? In addition to a breathable fabric, a removable and washable cover can help your blanket last. While some blankets already come with a machine-washable cover, others (like those with loops that attach to a duvet cover) may require you to purchase one separately. Meet our sleep experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Seema Khosla is the medical director of the North Dakota Center for Sleep. Lynelle Schneeberg is a board-certified sleep psychologist and author of “Become Your Child's Sleep Coach.” Dr. Schneeberg is an assistant professor at the Yale School of Medicine, the director of the behavioral sleep program at Connecticut Children’s Medical Center and a fellow of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. Michael Urban is an occupational therapy practitioner, senior lecturer and director of the Doctorate of Occupational Therapy Program at the University of New Haven. Dr. Alex Dimitriu is a board-certified psychiatrist and sleep medicine specialist at SiliconPsych. articles.title: Iran retaliates after US strikes, defying Trump’s warning it could be hit ‘much harder’
articles.summary: The US military carried out additional strikes Tuesday on Iran, prompting Tehran to attack Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in defiance of a warning from President Donald Trump that Iran would be “hit much harder” if it retaliated.
articles.body: The US military carried out additional strikes Tuesday on Iran, prompting Tehran to attack Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in defiance of a warning from President Donald Trump that Iran would be “hit much harder” if it retaliated. The latest round of tit-for-tat strikes began after the US and Iran traded attacks overnight into Monday for the first time in over a month, in exchanges that risked reigniting the damaging conflict after weeks of relative military calm. After the fresh US strikes were announced, Trump warned that Iran would face more severe military action if it retaliated against what he called a “very justified attack.” “They will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!” he wrote Tuesday on Truth Social. Iran, however, vowed a “crushing” response and launched ballistic missiles toward Jordan and drones toward Bahrain and Kuwait, saying it was targeting US military assets. Tehran claimed that shrapnel from one of the US strikes hit a wedding celebration in the country’s south, killing at least four people, including a toddler. In a statement to CNN, a US military spokesperson said US Central Command (CENTCOM) has seen reports about the claim and denied targeting civilians in Iran. “We are aware of reports, which originated from Iranian state media. The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” Capt. Timothy Hawkins, a CENTCOM spokesperson, said Wednesday, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The US strikes were in response to recent attempted Iranian attacks “against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and American troops deployed to the region,” CENTCOM said in a post on X. Since the US strikes on Sunday, two tankers have been struck by projectiles, according to maritime intelligence group Marisks and the traffic monitoring agency United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). Iran and the US are in a protracted battle over the narrow waterway, which is critical to global energy supplies. CENTCOM said Tuesday’s strikes targeted “air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine laying capabilities, and communications sites” associated with the IRGC. The strikes began at 12 p.m. ET, and CENTCOM announced they were complete more than six hours later. The flare-up in fighting occurred even though Trump previously telegraphed plans to shift away from a military campaign and toward a strategy focused on ramping up economic pressure. “I’m not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Tuesday night, after Iran retaliated. “I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing.” After the US announced the new strikes, oil futures climbed above $94 a barrel. On the diplomatic front, officials in Pakistan claimed they were “not discouraged” by the spike in violence. Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry “remains engaged” with Tehran and Washington, Tahir Andrabi, a spokesperson, told reporters Wednesday. He insisted that the strikes “should not be termed as a failure of the mediatory process.” What was targeted on Tuesday? Jordan said it intercepted 10 missiles from Iran, while three others fell in remote locations far from populated areas. No casualties were reported, Jordan’s military said. Kuwait and Bahrain said they also activated air defense systems intercepting drones from Iran. Tehran also claimed to have launched a combined missile and drone attack on Erbil in Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region. The US attacks, meanwhile, struck multiple locations across Iran. Seven people were killed in strikes on the central region of Khuzestan, which borders Iraq, the state-run Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported, citing a regional official. The neighboring Iranian port cities of Chabahar and Konarak on the Gulf of Oman, which host key commercial, maritime and military infrastructure, also came under attack. And explosions were heard east of Bandar Abbas and around Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, state-linked media said. Iran’s state-run Press TV said the strikes also hit the small regional Jiroft Airport in southeastern Iran and a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island in the strait. Separately, an explosion was heard in Iran’s southern county of Asaluyeh, a key gas and petrochemical hub on the Persian Gulf coast, according to Iran’s semi-official Fars News Agency. Shrapnel falls on wedding party Iranian authorities have claimed that several people, including a 4-year-old child, were killed and that at least 68 others were wounded when shrapnel fell on a building hosting a wedding celebration in the coastal village of Kouhestak in southern Iran’s Sirik county, according to Press TV. In footage released by Iran’s semi-official Tasnim News Agency, purporting to show the aftermath of a US strike, heavy smoke can be seen hanging in the air above rubble on the ground. All around, people can be heard shouting. CNN geolocated the imagery to a residential neighborhood in Kouhestak. A large communications tower in Kouhestak was also badly damaged on Tuesday night, video showed. The tower was located about 135 meters (442 feet) from the building hosting the wedding reception. At least 19 of the wounded were children under the age of 10, including seven boys and 12 girls, the Iranian Students’ News Agency quoted a regional health official as saying. Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, condemned the attack as part of a “catalogue of atrocities” committed by the US, and he criticized the global community’s “normalization of bombing.” Baghaei also denounced CENTCOM’s denial of targeting civilians in Iran, describing the strike as a “brutal war crime” in a post on X on Wednesday. The attack was covered widely across Iranian state media, prompting outrage on Iranian social media and the quick publication of a Lego-style animated video –– the kind that has become a mainstay of Iranian propaganda throughout the war. CNN has been unable to independently verify the details of the alleged strike. Kouhestak is just 37 kilometers (about 22 miles) from the city of Minab, where a US strike hit an elementary school in February, killing at least 168 children and 14 teachers, according to Iran. Strait of Hormuz will be ‘worthless piece of water’ The fighting resumed as the US and Iran remained locked in a struggle over the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran claims the right to control but the US says is an international waterway. The strait has been a chokepoint for global energy supplies since the war broke out, but in recent weeks more oil has been flowing through it. The US claimed that it launched its strikes on Sunday because Iran was trying to use rockets to plant new sea mines in the strait. Tehran responded by firing at what it called US military targets in the Middle East. Trump told Fox News on Tuesday that the US gave Arab allies in the Persian Gulf a heads-up before its latest strikes, and he criticized Iran’s leadership. “I think an agreement with them isn’t worth the paper it’s written on,” the president said, later adding: “They don’t stop: They’re crazy, and they’re stupid.” Trump told Fox that the US went after radar systems that Tehran had tried to rebuild. “They tried to rebuild their radar because they can’t see anything,” he said. “We waited until it was almost built, and then we hit it.” The Trump administration has repeatedly dismissed concerns about Iran’s long-term hold on the strait. “In two years, the Strait of Hormuz will be like a worthless piece of water — the oil will be going on pipelines across land,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Larry Kudlow on Tuesday during an interview at a Group of 20 meeting. He was referring to plans by Arab states in the gulf to build infrastructure that bypasses the strait completely. Bessent also claimed that the Treasury Department’s new push to cut off Iran’s economy from the rest of the world would eventually force the regime to surrender, characterizing his job as to “make sure that they want to have a deal.” “We are going to economically asphyxiate this regime,” Bessent said. “The world is tired of this pariah state, or this rogue state, and they are willing to make it a pariah.” He added that after initially targeting a bank in Dubai for its alleged ties to Iran, the Treasury Department is likely to sanction two more banks in the next couple weeks. This story has been updated with additional details. CNN’s Alejandra Jaramillo, Matt Egan, Aida Karimi, Hira Humayun, Eyad Kourdi, Azaz Syed and Kaanita Iyer contributed reporting.

articles.title: A woman was swimming in Lake Tahoe. Then she 'felt the teeth and claws'
articles.summary: The woman, a swim instructor, was left dripping in blood after being attacked in Lake Tahoe.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This story includes graphic photos that may be disturbing to some readers.

A routine morning swim in Lake Tahoe turned violent for one woman following an otter attack in Reno, Nevada.

The otter attacked Lynnette Bellin on Sunday, Aug. 30 underwater while she swam near Hidden Beach in Incline Village. The otter suddenly grabbed her leg and pulled her underwater, she told the Reno Gazette Journal , part of the USA TODAY Network.

As a result, Bellin was left with cuts all over her face, arm and legs and required 22 stitches and a rabies vaccination.

"At first I thought it was a person pulling on me because it was so strong," Bellin told the Gazette Journal on Monday, Aug. 31.

"I haven't seen anyone else out there swimming, so I wasn't sure," she said. "And then I felt the teeth and claws, and it was relentless.

She then turned around and spotted the otter, which was biting and scratching her. As the attack continued, Bellin tried to reach a nearby set of rocks and even threw the otter.

Though she yelled for help, no one responded. Still, she managed to exit the water using a set of rocks.

Once back at the beach, Bellin saw the otter circling the area and drove herself to the hospital.

Photos of Bellin's injuries taken after the incident showed Bellin with blood running down her face and left arm and hand. She'd been swimming in the area since July and is a professional swim instructor but has never experienced anything like what happened in Lake Tahoe.

The Washoe County Sheriff's Office, which responded to the incident, searched for the animal on Aug. 30 but was unable to locate it, the Nevada Department of Wildlife told the Gazette Journal.

The incident marks the second otter attack this summer at Lake Tahoe.

Bob Daly was swimming at Pope Beach on Aug. 9 when an otter attacked him, leaving him with eight bloody bite and scratch marks, according to South Tahoe Now .

There was also an otter attack in Anchorage, Alaska, KTUU reported last month.

Lake Tahoe is home to Northern river otters.

The creatures are nocturnal but may be active in the early morning and later afternoon in remote areas, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture .

Populations are listed as stable or increasing in Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Rhode Island, Texas, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin, per the agency.

Otter attacks can be dangerous but are rare for the most part. According to the Otter Specialist Group , which conducted a review of otter attacks in 2011, only 39 attacks have been documented since 1875.

North American otters were most likely to be involved in attacks. The greatest number of attacks were documented in Florida.

Otter attacks have also been reported in British Columbia, California, Georgia, Iowa, Massachusetts, Montana, Montana, New Hampshire, New York, Oregon, Vermont, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin.

Michelle Del Rey is a trending news reporter at USA TODAY. Reach her at mdelrey@usatoday.com.

articles.title: SC abre concurso público com 50 vagas e salário de R$ 25,3 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidades exigem ensino superior em cinco áreas. Inscrições começam às 10h de sexta-feira (4) e provas ocorrem em novembro.
articles.summary: O concurso Sefaz-SC oferece vagas para auditor em cinco áreas de nível superior, com inscrições abertas a partir desta sexta-feira e provas previstas para novembro.
articles.body:
Ponte Hercílio Luz — Foto: Prefeitura de Florianópolis

A Secretaria de Estado da Fazenda de Santa Catarina (Sefaz-SC) publicou, na terça-feira (1º), edital para concurso público com 50 vagas imediatas , além de cadastro de reserva, com salário inicial de R$ 25.337,61.

As oportunidades são para auditor estadual de finanças públicas , para uma jornada de trabalho de 40 horas semanais.

📍 Os aprovados trabalharão na sede da Sefaz-SC, em Florianópolis , e serão contratados sob o regime do Estatuto dos Servidores Públicos Civis do Estado de Santa Catarina. Eles passarão por estágio probatório.

Para concorrer, é necessário ter ensino superior completo na área de atuação escolhida. A banca organizadora do certame é a Fundação Carlos Chagas (FCC) .

As 50 vagas imediatas estão divididas em cinco áreas de conhecimento . Do total de oportunidades, 5% são reservadas para pessoas com deficiência (PCD).

🔎Veja a distribuição das vagas e formação exigida

Ciências contábeis : 20 vagas (19 para ampla concorrência e 1 para PCD);

Tecnologia da informação (ciências da computação, engenharia de software, engenharia de computação, sistemas de informação ou licenciatura em computação): 12 vagas (11 para ampla concorrência e 1 para PCD);

Direito: 8 vagas (7 para ampla concorrência e 1 para PCD);

Administração e engenharias: 6 vagas (5 para ampla concorrência e 1 para PCD);

Ciências econômicas : 4 vagas (3 para ampla concorrência e 1 para PCD).

Governo de SC publica edital de concurso com 50 vagas e salário inicial de R$ 25,3 mil; — Foto: Governo de SC/Divulgação

Período de inscrição: entre 10h de sexta-feira (4) e 23h59 de 5 de outubro de 2026.

Onde se inscrever? No site da Fundação Carlos Chagas (FCC).

Os candidatos podem solicitar a isenção da taxa entre os dias 4 e 8 de setembro de 2026 . O benefício é voltado para:

Doadores de sangue, medula óssea ou leite humano;

Eleitores convocados pela Justiça Eleitoral;

Pessoas de baixa renda (hipossuficiência financeira).

As provas objetivas serão aplicadas no dia 22 de novembro de 2026, em Florianópolis, e divididas em dois turnos:

Manhã (4 horas de duração) : Prova objetiva (Conhecimentos Gerais), com 80 questões de múltipla escolha.

Tarde (5 horas de duração) : Prova objetiva (Conhecimentos Específicos), com 100 questões.

Para todas as áreas, a prova de conhecimentos gerais terá questões de língua portuguesa, matemática financeira, estatística, raciocínio lógico, ciência e análise de dados, ética e integridade, e conhecimentos regionais de Santa Catarina.

O concurso terá validade de dois anos, contados a partir da homologação do resultado final, e poderá ser prorrogado uma única vez por igual período.

articles.title: Executiva morta na Times Square era mãe de uma bebê de 5 meses | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataque também deixou um homem de 68 anos ferido, segundo a polícia. Mulher suspeita de cometer o crime tinha histórico de problemas de saúde mental e foi morta.
articles.summary: Ataque também deixou um homem de 68 anos ferido, segundo a polícia. Mulher suspeita de cometer o crime tinha histórico de problemas de saúde mental e foi morta.
articles.body:
Erin Piacenti, de 32 anos, vice-presidente do Bank of America que morreu num ataque a faca na região da Times Square, em Nova York , havia dado à lua a uma menina cinco meses antes e havia acabado de voltar ao trabalho após sua licença-maternidade.

A executiva foi morta em um ataque aparentemente aleatório e sem motivo , afirmaram autoridades que investigam o caso na terça-feira (1º).

Piacentini, vice-presidente da área de seleção de negócios e conflitos de interesses do banco, estava em sua primeira semana de retorno ao trabalho. Recentemente, ela havia feito um post em suas redes sociais sobre se sentir grata por ter passado os últimos meses com a filha recém-nascida, segundo o jornal "The New York Times".

A reportagem do "NYT" afirma que ela estava próxima à bilheteria quando foi atacada pela mulher de 49 anos, a qual aparentava estar em surto. Ela chegou a ser levada ao hospital Bellevue, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos.

Em comunicado, o Bank of America lamentou a morte da funcionária.

“Estamos chocados e profundamente tristes com a trágica perda de nossa colega. Ela era uma colega de equipe muito valorizada, de quem sentiremos muita falta. Nossos pensamentos estão com sua família e todos os seus entes queridos”, afirmou o banco.

O escritório do Bank of America em Manhattan fica a poucos passos da Times Square. O banco também possui outros centros financeiros espalhados pela cidade de Nova York, um dos principais centros financeiros dos Estados Unidos .

Erin se formou em direito pela Fordham Law School em 2021, com o marido, Frank Piacenti, segundo a universidade de Nova York. Em comunicado, a instituição afirmou estar profundamente abalada com a morte da ex-aluna.

Vice-presidente do Bank of America Erin Piacenti e autora de ataque com faca na Times Square — Foto: Reprodução

A suspeita de atacar a executiva, Pamela Cisneros, de 49 anos, foi morta por policiais minutos após o ataque. Antes de atacar Erin, ela esfaqueou um homem de 68 anos, que sobreviveu e está em condição estável.

Segundo a polícia, Pamela tinha histórico de problemas de saúde mental.

O irmão dela, Patrick Peralta, afirmou ao site de notícias de Nova York Gothamist que a mulher enfrentava problemas psiquiátricos havia décadas, mas não era agressiva.

Segundo ele, Pamela era divorciada e mãe de três filhos. O homem disse que a mulher tomava medicamentos e vinha apresentando melhora nos últimos anos.

Peralta afirmou ainda que a irmã trabalhava de forma intermitente em um escritório de advocacia e que a viu pela última vez no início de agosto, durante uma reunião de família para comemorar um aniversário.

Segundo ele, Pamela conversou com a própria mãe, por telefone, no sábado e disse que estava bem. Dois dias depois, a família sobre do ataque pela televisão.

“Realmente não sabemos como expressar ou explicar por que isso aconteceu”, disse ele ao Gothamist, ao manifestar solidariedade à família de Erin e ao homem ferido.

Polícia de Nova York interditou área da Times Square após mulher esfaquear duas pessoas e ser baleada — Foto: Angela Weiss/AFP

Segundo a comissária da Polícia de Nova York, Jessica Tisch, Pamela retirou duas facas de uma sacola de compras, esfaqueou o homem e, em seguida, atacou Piacenti.

Vídeos feitos por pessoas que estavam no local mostram policiais cercando a suspeita enquanto ela segurava duas facas grandes. As imagens mostram que, quando os agentes usaram um taser, ela balançou as facas e caminhou rapidamente na direção dos policiais.

Diante da ameaça, dois policiais atiraram contra a mulher, segundo a polícia.

Tisch afirmou que os agentes tentaram convencer a mulher a largar as facas durante vários minutos antes de usar o taser. Segundo ela, a suspeita disse que não largaria as armas e que “preferia matar” os policiais.

“A investigação continua a cargo da Divisão de Investigação da Força da Polícia de Nova York”, informou a NYPD em comunicado.

Luigi Mangione é acusado de matar o CEO da UnitedHealthcare, em Nova York, em dezembro de 2024 — Foto: Steven Hirsch/Pool via REUTERS

O caso aconteceu após um alto executivo da Blackstone ser morto a tiros no ano passado, quando um atirador armado com um fuzil invadiu o saguão de um prédio de luxo no centro de Manhattan e abriu fogo.

No fim de 2024, o então CEO da UnitedHealthcare, Brian Thompson, foi morto a tiros ao sair de um hotel em Nova York . O suspeito, Luigi Mangione, foi preso dias depois, em um caso que repercutiu em todo o mundo.

Em 2022, um funcionário de 48 anos do Goldman Sachs foi baleado e morto em um ataque aleatório e sem motivo aparente enquanto viajava de trem do Brooklyn para Lower Manhattan.

Os índices de criminalidade de Nova York vêm sendo alvo de atenção há anos. No mês passado, a NYPD informou ter registrado os menores números de tiroteios, vítimas de tiroteios e homicídios nos primeiros sete meses do ano e também no mês de julho.

articles.title: Ônibus pega fogo na Tamoios: Contorno Sul é bloqueado em São Sebastião | G1
articles.standfirst: Incêndio aconteceu na altura do km 28 do Contorno Sul, no sentido Ubatuba. Trecho fica em São Sebastião.
articles.summary: Um ônibus pegou fogo no km 28 do Contorno Sul da Rodovia dos Tamoios, sentido Ubatuba, mobilizando bombeiros e interditando o tráfego no túnel nesta quarta-feira.
articles.body:
Um ônibus pegou fogo próximo a um túnel da Rodovia dos Tamoios, em São Sebastião , no Litoral Norte de São Paulo, na tarde desta quarta-feira (2).

Segundo a Concessionária Tamoios, o incêndio começou por volta das 12h50, na altura do km 28 do Contorno Sul, no sentido Ubatuba.

Ônibus pegou fogo no Contorno Sul, em São Sebastião. — Foto: Concessionária Tamoios

Equipes da concessionária e do Corpo de Bombeiros foram ao local e atenderam a ocorrência. O trecho permaneceu interditado nos dois sentidos por cerca de uma hora antes de ser deixado em segurança.

Por sorte, ninguém ficou ferido. Ainda não se sabe o que causou o incêndio. O trecho foi liberado por volta das 14h30 e o tráfego de veículos foi normalizado no local.

articles.standfirst: Palestra com Renata Cavinato abordará atitude, resiliência, performance e produtividade para impulsionar resultados.
articles.summary: Palestra com Renata Cavinato abordará atitude, resiliência, performance e produtividade para impulsionar resultados.
articles.body:
Café do Conhecimento em setembro aborda o tema “Movimento Gera Resultado” — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

O Conselho da Mulher Empreendedora, o CME da ACIL, promove, no dia 24 de setembro, mais uma edição do Café da Manhã do Conhecimento, encontro que reúne empresários, profissionais, convidados e empreendedores em uma manhã dedicada à troca de experiências e à busca por novos conhecimentos. Desta vez, o tema será “Movimento Gera Resultado”, com palestra de Renata Cavinato.

O evento acontece na ACIL e terá início às 8h, com o coffee, seguido pela palestra, às 8h30. Coreógrafa, bailarina, professora de dança, palestrante e ginasta, Renata levará para o ambiente empresarial uma abordagem dinâmica sobre a importância de sair da inércia, movimentar ideias e transformar atitudes em resultados.

Ao longo da palestra, serão trabalhados temas que conectam movimento, comportamento e desempenho profissional. Entre os tópicos estão “A Arte de Sair da Inércia”, “O Efeito Dominó nos Negócios”, “Evolução Coletiva e Resiliência” e “Energia, Performance e Alta Produtividade”.

Mais do que uma palestra, o encontro busca proporcionar aos participantes uma experiência de aprendizado e reflexão sobre como atitudes, movimento e engajamento podem contribuir para a evolução pessoal e coletiva dentro das empresas.

O investimento para participar é de R$ 15 para associados da ACIL e R$ 35 para não associados. As vagas são limitadas.

O Café da Manhã do Conhecimento é uma oportunidade para começar o dia ampliando conhecimentos, fortalecendo conexões e encontrando novas perspectivas para transformar movimento em resultado. O evento acontece toda última quinta-feira do mês, na ACIL.

articles.title: GCM amplia atuação e registra 158 prisões em flagrante no primeiro semestre | G1
articles.standfirst: Em 2025, o aumento do efetivo ocorreu somente a partir de setembro, enquanto neste ano a estrutura reforçada já atua desde o primeiro semestre em São Sebastião
articles.summary: Em 2025, o aumento do efetivo ocorreu somente a partir de setembro, enquanto neste ano a estrutura reforçada já atua desde o primeiro semestre em São Sebastião
articles.body:
O reforço dos investimentos da Prefeitura de São Sebastião em segurança urbana amplia a presença e a capacidade de resposta da Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM). Entre janeiro e junho de 2026, as equipes registraram 158 prisões em flagrante, número que já representa aproximadamente 92% das 171 contabilizadas durante todo o ano de 2025.

O resultado acompanha a ampliação da estrutura da segurança municipal promovida pela Prefeitura, com reforço do efetivo, que vai chegar a cerca de 136 agentes, novas viaturas, maior presença das equipes nas ruas e investimentos em tecnologia e monitoramento. Em 2025, o aumento do efetivo ocorreu somente a partir de setembro, enquanto neste ano a estrutura reforçada já atua desde o primeiro semestre.

Os dados da Secretaria de Segurança Urbana (Segur) mostram também a diversidade das ocorrências atendidas pela GCM. Nos primeiros seis meses de 2026, foram registrados 46 furtos, sete roubos e 64 ocorrências relacionadas ao tráfico de entorpecentes, além das 158 prisões em flagrante.

Comparado com os seis primeiros meses de 2025, foram 49 furtos e roubos, 30 apreensão de drogas e 85 prisões em flagrante. O que mostra que as ações da GCM vem aumentando gradualmente no combate à criminalidade.

Para a administração municipal, o crescimento no número de prisões em flagrante deve ser analisado também sob a perspectiva do aumento da capacidade operacional da GCM. Com mais agentes, canil e viaturas nas ruas, o município amplia o patrulhamento preventivo, as abordagens e a resposta às ocorrências.

A atuação nas ruas é complementada pelo investimento em tecnologia. São Sebastião conta com sistema de videomonitoramento e Muralha Eletrônica, ferramentas que auxiliam as equipes na identificação de veículos, localização de procurados pela Justiça, acompanhamento de ocorrências e apoio às demais forças de segurança.

A integração é outro eixo do trabalho desenvolvido no município. A GCM atua em apoio às polícias Civil e Militar e demais órgãos de segurança, compartilhando informações e recursos tecnológicos sempre que necessário.

articles.title: Elizabete Arrabaça diz ser inocente e acusa filha mais velha de mentir | G1
articles.standfirst: Audiência de instrução ocorreu na segunda-feira (31), e a ré, que está presa em Tremembé, foi ouvida de forma virtual. Segundo ela, Viviane Garnica quer prejudicá-la.
articles.summary: Audiência de instrução ocorreu na segunda-feira (31), e a ré, que está presa em Tremembé, foi ouvida de forma virtual. Segundo ela, Viviane Garnica quer prejudicá-la.
articles.body:
Ré no processo que investiga a morte da filha mais nova, Nathália Garnica , Elizabete Arrabaça afirmou em depoimento na segunda-feira (31) que é inocente e não cometeu o crime que é acusada.

"Eu sou inocente. Eu juro por Pai, Filho e Espírito Santo que eu sou inocente. Tudo isso é mentira. Eu sou inocente. Eu sou inocente. Com essa luz, eu quero que me cega se eu tiver mentindo".

Durante o depoimento, ela também disse que a filha mais velha, Viviane Garnica, mentiu ao juiz em audiência de instrução e julgamento para prejudicá-la.

"Ela está querendo me prejudicar, muita coisa ela distorceu no depoimento dela, inventou muita coisa. E eu fiquei muito triste, muito triste. Família sabe como é, né? A única que cuidava muito bem de mim era a Nathália".

Elizabete está presa na Penitenciária de Tremembé desde o dia 20 de agosto do ano passado, por conta da morte da nora, a professora de pilates Larissa Rodrigues. A ré foi ouvida de forma virtual.

À EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, o advogado de defesa de Elizabete, Bruno Ribeiro, disse que a ré é inocente.

"Ela não só acredita, como ela é inocente. O que o Ministério Público tentou trazer ao longo da investigação policial, a polícia, e o Ministério Público agora, em fase judicial, tentar reproduzir esses indícios como provas, ao ver da defesa, isso não foi feito. O Ministério Público tenta importar aquela mesma alegação do processo Larissa de dificuldades financeiras e de vício em jogos para justificar algum interesse financeiro dela em uma eventual herança da filha".

Elizabete Arrabaça diz que filha mais velha mentiu em depoimento que investiga morte de Nathália Garnica, em Pontal (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TJSP

Nathália e Larissa foram mortas com um veneno popularmente conhecido como 'chumbinho', mas as substâncias administradas para cada uma das vítimas são diferentes, de acordo com laudos toxicológicos.

Os processos correm separadamente, uma vez que os crimes foram em cidades diferentes (Nathália morreu em Pontal e Larissa, em Ribeirão Preto ). Os julgamentos ainda não têm data para ocorrer.

Nathália Garnica m orreu aos 42 anos, no dia 9 de fevereiro de 2025, em Pontal, onde morava . Um dia antes, Elizabete Arrabaça esteve com a filha na casa dela. À época, o boletim de ocorrência chegou a ser registrado como morte natural.

Quando as investigações sobre a morte da cunhada, Larissa Rodrigues, começaram, um laudo toxicológico apontou que a professora tinha sido envenenada com chumbinho. Elizabete e Luiz Antônio Garnica, irmão de Nathália, foram presos no dia 6 de maio , por suspeita de participação na morte de Larissa.

Como o intervalo de tempo entre os dois casos era curto, a polícia passou a investigar também a morte de Nathália. No dia 23 de maio, o corpo dela foi exumado para ser analisado.

No dia 17 de junho, o laudo toxicológico confirmou que Nathália também tinha morrido envenenada por chumbinho.

Por conta da similaridade dos casos e também por ter sido a última pessoa a estar com as duas vítimas, Elizabete, que já era investigada pela morte da nora, Larissa , passou a ser investigada pela morte da filha, Nathália.

articles.title: Tiger Woods se declara culpado por acidente de trânsito | G1
articles.standfirst: Astro do golfe se envolveu em um acidente na Flórida em março e chegou a ser preso por estar 'alterado' durante abordagem, segundo a polícia. Woods fez um acordo judicial e se livrou de acusações de dirigir sob efeito de entorpecentes.
articles.summary: Astro do golfe se envolveu em um acidente na Flórida em março e chegou a ser preso por estar 'alterado' durante abordagem, segundo a polícia. Woods fez um acordo judicial e se livrou de acusações de dirigir sob efeito de entorpecentes.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods acompanhado de sua namorada, Vanessa Trump, ao deixar tribunal após se declarar culpado por direção imprudente em 2 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Marco Bello

Tiger Woods se declarou culpado nesta quarta-feira (2) das acusações de direção imprudente e descuidada, decorrentes de um acidente de carro com capotamento ocorrido em março na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos .

Woods fez um acordo com a Justiça norte-americana para que fosse retirada a acusação de dirigir sob influência de álcool ou drogas, a mais grave que ele enfrentava. Isso fez com que ele mudasse sua posição no processo judicial, já que anteriormente ele havia se declarado inocente.

Mesmo assim, o astro do golfe terá a carteira de motorista suspensa por cinco anos , segundo o acordo judicial.

Woods foi preso no final de março após capotar seu carro em colisão com um reboque . Ele estava "alterado" no momento da abordagem, segundo os policiais, o que fez com que as autoridades levantassem suspeitas de direção sob efeito de entorpecentes.

O jogador de golfe compareceu a uma audiência nesta quarta em um tribunal regional em Stuart, na Flórida, onde se declarou culpado perante um juiz.

articles.title: Nearly 2,000-year-old vessel with two snake heads found at a Roman villa in Spain; archaeologists link it to the secretive cult of Sabazios
articles.summary: Europe News: At the Roman villa of Collet, on a low cliff above Spain's Bay of Palamós, archaeologists have uncovered fragments of a large ceramic vessel that appe.
articles.body: At the Roman villa of Collet, on a low cliff above Spain's Bay of Palamós, archaeologists have uncovered fragments of a large ceramic vessel that appears to reveal one of the empire's more secretive religious practices. Its handle, moulded into a two-headed serpent covered in tiny incised scales, was broken and buried close to a bread oven sometime during the Augustan period, roughly two thousand years ago. Researchers now argue the piece belonged to the cult of Sabazios, a Thracian and Phrygian god whose worship in the Roman world rarely left the home. Evidence for the cult on the Iberian Peninsula is thin, mostly clustered near the ancient city of Emporiae, making the Collet find a rare rural example. Laboratory testing of the vessel's clay points further still, suggesting it may have travelled from Roman Africa rather than being made locally, hinting at how far the cult's quiet influence could reach.What does the snake-headed vessel revealThe fragments were recovered from the Roman villa of Collet, which sits on a rocky outcrop roughly 20 metres above the Bay of Palamós, in the ancient territory linking the ciuitates of Gerunda and Emporiae. According to the study published by Cambridge University Press, titled ‘Of snakes and gods: early evidence for the cult of Sabazios in the Roman villa of Collet’, the site was first identified in the late nineteenth century. Still, it was not properly excavated until the early 2000s, with work on the villa itself beginning in 2015. Archaeologists have since traced five distinct phases of activity at Collet, starting with a modest rural settlement built around a wine cellar and grain store at the end of the second or start of the first century BC.The snake-decorated fragments turned up just outside the villa's east wall, in a layer connected to the construction of a bread oven during the Augustan period. The surrounding pottery, including Baetican and Tarraconensis amphorae, fragments of grey Emporitan ware and a piece of Italian terra sigillata, confirms that the vessel was already broken and buried by this time. A second wave of finds from the oven's period of use, including a cup of Italian terra sigillata and a slightly later amphora style, pin the deposit firmly to the first half of the first century AD.Why does the vessel have two snake headsWhat survives of the vessel is only part of its everted rim and a single handle, but the decoration leaves little doubt about its intended purpose. The handle bears a coarse but elaborate design showing a snake with a head at each end, meeting the rim on either side, its body covered in small semi-circular incisions meant to suggest overlapping scales. Simple incised eyes and a moulded line marking the mouth give the two serpent heads a somewhat stylised, though still recognisable, form.Researchers compared the shape to a known typology of Sabazios-linked vessels from Germania and Belgica, established by the scholar M. Amand, though the Collet piece does not fully match that classification. The fragments lack the pouring spout typical of that type, and their decoration more closely resembles examples recorded at Carnuntum in Austria, albeit vessels believed to be later and produced in workshops in northern Gaul. Because the body of the vessel was never recovered, the researchers stop short of assigning it to any established category, describing it instead as a distinctive, if related, local variant.Who was Sabazios and how was his cult worshippedSabazios was a god of the Thracian and Phrygian peoples of the Balkans, and his worship in the Roman world stayed largely private, practised within households rather than in public shrines. One of the clearest parallels comes from a house in Pompeii, where a small brick altar in a garden courtyard was found alongside two terracotta vessels decorated with snakes and toads, motifs closely associated with the god. Because the cult relied on symbolic objects such as bronze hands, small plaques and specific ceramic bowls rather than temples or inscriptions, tracing its spread depends heavily on recognising this recurring imagery.Evidence for the cult on the Iberian Peninsula remains sparse, largely confined to its northern edge. A bronze bust interpreted as a Sabazios figure was found at l'Alcúdia near Elche, a bronze hand recovered off Cartagena is thought to have come from a shipwreck, and a possible sanctuary at the Cueva Negra site in Murcia remains disputed among scholars. The strongest evidence lies near Empúries, the ancient city of Emporiae, where an Augustan-era tomb produced a triptych of bronze plaques depicting Sabazios and the twin gods Castor and Pollux, suggesting an itinerant priest may once have carried the cult inland from the coast.How did researchers trace the vessel’s possible African originExamination of the ceramic paste under a binocular microscope revealed a compact, well-fired red fabric containing quartz, mica and small white mineral nodules likely formed from altered calcium carbonate, while x-ray diffraction confirmed the presence of feldspar alongside these zeolite-like deposits. A trace of white slip on the fragment's surface, made from the same finely ground minerals, further set the piece apart from pottery produced at the nearby Collet Est workshop.These traits point away from a local Catalan origin and towards production somewhere in Roman Africa, even though comparable Sabazios vessels are almost unknown there. Only a single similar vessel of Tunisian origin, held in a German museum collection and undated, offers even a loose parallel. The researchers conclude that the Collet fragment represents an early rural example of Iberian "serpent-ware," suggesting that even a minor, intimate cult such as that of Sabazios could travel far beyond the cities where it first took root, reaching quietly into the countryside of the western provinces.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra: Operation Sindoor commander, war medal awardee and now Ram Temple's first CEO
articles.summary: AYODHYA: Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra (Retd), who commanded the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, has been a.
articles.body: AYODHYA: Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra (Retd), who commanded the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, has been appointed the first chief executive officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.The appointment was announced during the trust's meeting in Ayodhya on Wednesday, which had earlier announced the appointment of three new trustees: Delhi-based Mahesh Bhagchandka, a relative of late VHP leader Ashok Singhal; Ayodhya-based Madan Mohan Pandey; and retired Hindi professor Nirmala Yadav of Shikohabad.The CEO appointment assumes significance as the trust moves to strengthen the administrative and financial management of the Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, months after a controversy over alleged irregularities and embezzlement in the handling of temple donations and related financial management systems.Air Marshal Jitendra Mishra brings nearly four decades of experience in the Indian Air Force to the post.Commissioned as a fighter pilot in December 1986, he has logged more than 3,000 flying hours and served in several key operational, testing and strategic positions.He was both a fighter combat leader and an experimental test pilot, and served as the commanding officer of a fighter squadron, commander of two frontline air bases and chief test pilot at the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment (ASTE).Mishra later served as Commandant of ASTE and deputy chief of Integrated Defence Staff (Doctrine, Organisation and Training).At Air Headquarters, he held key positions including director of Operational Planning and Assessment, principal director (ASR) and assistant chief of Air Staff (Projects).In January 2025, Mishra took charge as Commander-in-Chief of the IAF's Western Air Command, a strategically important position responsible for India's western borders. He commanded the formation during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.For his service during the operation, Mishra was awarded the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal, a prestigious military decoration awarded for distinguished service during conflict.Mishra retired from the IAF in April 2026. He is originally from Bhopatpura in Uttar Pradesh's Deoria district and comes from a middle-class family. His father was a lecturer.A graduate of the National Defence Academy in Pune, Mishra also underwent advanced training at the Air Force Test Pilots School in Bengaluru, the Air Command and Staff College in the United States and the Royal College of Defence Studies in the United Kingdom.His appointment as the first CEO gives the Ram Temple Trust an administrator with extensive experience in military leadership, strategic planning, operations and institutional management at a time when the Trust is expanding its administrative structure.Meet first Ram Temple CEOOperation Sindoor commander: Mishra commanded the IAF's Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.First Ram Temple CEO: He has been appointed the first CEO of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal awardee: He received the prestigious Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal for distinguished service during conflict.Joined IAF in 1986: Mishra was commissioned as a fighter pilot in December 1986 and retired in April 2026.3,000+ flying hours: He has logged more than 3,000 hours of flying during his IAF career.Fighter and test pilot: He served as both a fighter combat leader and experimental test pilot.Frontline command experience: His career included command of a fighter squadron and two frontline air bases.Senior strategic roles: Mishra served as Commandant of ASTE and Deputy Chief of Integrated Defence Staff, besides holding several key positions at Air Headquarters.Elite military training: He is an NDA graduate and trained at institutions in India, the US and the UK.Roots in eastern UP: Mishra hails from Bhopatpura in Deoria district, relatively close to Ayodhya, and comes from a middle-class family. articles.title: U.S. may ask parents to prove citizenship or immigration status to get passports for children
articles.summary: The U.S. State Department has proposed requiring parents applying for passports for their ​children to provide proof of their own citizenship or immigration status as part of President Donald Trump’s latest effort to limit birthright ‌citizenship.
articles.body: The U.S. State Department has proposed requiring parents applying for passports for their ​children to provide proof of their own citizenship or immigration status as part of President Donald Trump’s latest effort to limit birthright ‌citizenship. The draft guidance, reviewed by Reuters, is the first detailed look at how the State Department could enforce Trump’s August 6 executive order targeting what it calls “birth tourism” and broadening historical exceptions to birthright citizenship. The White House referred Reuters questions to the State Department. In a statement, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said that “President Trump has been unequivocal that ​this Administration will protect the meaning and value of American citizenship, full stop, and that includes making sure our passport adjudication process fully ​reflects that standard.” Limiting birthright citizenship has been one of the president’s top priorities in his far-reaching crackdown on immigration. The ⁠U.S. Supreme Court ruled his previous attempt violated the country’s Constitution. Trump’s initial executive order would have granted automatic U.S. citizenship at birth only to children ​with at least one parent who was a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident known as a green card holder. In a 6-3 ruling, the Supreme ​Court found the order was unlawful, with a majority finding it violated the Citizenship Clause of the Constitution’s 14th Amendment. Implementing Trump’s order Trump’s August 6 order was narrower, taking particular aim at “birth tourism,” in which women travel to the United States to give birth so their children can obtain automatic citizenship. That order could still be blocked in court. The ​new directive would withhold citizenship from children with a parent who works for a foreign government in the U.S., is engaged in fraud or a ​commercial transaction to obtain citizenship, or is classified as an “alien enemy.” “The Department will require parental information and evidence of parental citizenship or immigration status as part of its determination ‌whether the ⁠applicant is subject to EO 14418,” the State Department draft guidance reads, citing the executive order number. If implemented, the proposal would require all parents or legal guardians to provide proof of their citizenship, such as a valid U.S. passport or birth certificate, or evidence of their immigration status, such as an I-94 form or a legal permanent residency card, when submitting a passport application for their children. The information would be used by the government to determine if the ​child qualifies for citizenship under the ​new order, the State Department proposal ⁠says. Currently, parents whose children were born in the U.S. only need to prove their parentage and present photo identification during this process. They are also asked to check a box on the application form indicating if they are ​U.S. citizens but are not required to file supporting documentation. Lawyers pursuing class-action lawsuits on behalf of babies who would ​be deprived of citizenship ⁠under Trump’s initial order have asked two different federal judges to prevent his latest order from taking effect. One of those lawsuits is before U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman, who was appointed by Democratic President Joe Biden. At a hearing on Friday in Greenbelt, Maryland, Boardman voiced skepticism about what she called Trump’s unprecedented order and ⁠allowed the ​plaintiffs to revise their lawsuit so she could consider whether to block it. Justice Department attorneys have ​argued that a restraining order would be inappropriate and that the legal challenge was premature, as federal agencies had yet to issue public guidance on how the president’s directive would be implemented.

articles.title: Putin and Zelenskyy issue threats as strikes rock Ukraine, Russia
articles.summary: Putin accuses Zelenskyy of ‘terrorism’, while Ukraine warns foreign airlines against using Russian airspace.
articles.body:
Russian drone attacks across Ukraine have killed at least one person and wounded more than a dozen others, as Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Vladimir Putin threatened to escalate the conflict.

Between Tuesday and Wednesday, Ukrainian authorities reported attacks in the capital, Kyiv, in the southern city of Odesa and in eastern Dnipro, where the body of a man was retrieved from under rubble.

The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as the conflict stretches into its fifth year following Moscow’s invasion of its neighbour. The front line in eastern and southern Ukraine remains largely deadlocked, and US efforts to negotiate a peace settlement have yet to produce a path to peace.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy exchanged threats late on Tuesday over what their next steps might be.

Zelenskyy warned foreign airlines that the skies over Russia are not safe for flights due to Ukrainian long-range drone attacks, saying that “Russian airspace will effectively be closing”. He said Ukrainian military pressure aims to compel Russia to accept peace negotiations.

Putin accused Zelenskyy of “state terrorism” and said: “We don’t negotiate with terrorists.”

At a late-night news conference on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, Putin also addressed reports that the Ukrainian military had used British-made drones to strike targets inside Russia.

Asked whether Russia would strike British military facilities if the UK government continues to provide Ukraine with weaponry, Putin declined to rule it out. With a small smile, he told reporters it was “a military secret”.

China and North Korea, meanwhile, have provided military support for Russia, as has Iran in previous years.

The Russian and Ukrainian leaders’ comments came as European officials weigh their response to the latest in what they say is Moscow’s campaign of continental sabotage and disruption aimed at weakening European support for Ukraine. Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle airport last month using a drone laden with explosives.

Russia fired 174 attack drones, about half of them jet-powered drones that are hard to stop and are increasingly being deployed by Moscow, as well as two ballistic missiles and two plane-launched missiles at Ukraine overnight, according to the Ukrainian Air Force.

Officials in the southern Ukraine region of Odesa reported that the attack damaged a 24-storey residential building, destroying apartments on several floors and wounding eight people, including a child.

Odesa office buildings and two educational facilities were also damaged, Serhiy Lysak, head of the Odesa city military administration, said. The barrage also caused a power outage that halted electric-powered public transport, the city council said.

A man and a woman were wounded by shrapnel in morning attacks on the Kyiv region, according to Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration.

It was the seventh straight day Kyiv came under attack, although the latest barrage wasn’t as heavy as in previous days. The assault started a fire at a warehouse, officials said. Russian forces have targeted civilian facilities in what Ukrainian officials say is an effort to disrupt daily life and sap public morale.

A fire broke out at an educational facility and a medical practice was also damaged, the Kyiv city military administration said.

Meanwhile in Russia, air defences destroyed 130 Ukrainian drones overnight, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday. The drones were shot down over 11 Russian regions, as well as the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea, it said.

Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people in Russia’s Belgorod border region and wounded 16 more, acting governor Aleksand Shuvaev said. Ukrainian forces hit the region 140 times over the course of 24 hours, he said.

Ukraine’s domestically developed long-range drones have repeatedly targeted Russia’s oil sector, hoping to dent the economy and the warehouses of online retailers to make the Russian public feel the effects of war.

articles.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Leipzig
articles.summary: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.
articles.body:
The heads of Nato and the European Commission have warned that Russia is growing increasingly reckless and vowed to respond to a "new normal".

"Leipzig marks a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia," said Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, a day after Germany blamed Russia for a failed drone attack last month on Leipzig airport.

"We have to step up and that means being ready to respond to Russia's recklessness faster and better," von der Leyen said. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte said the whole alliance, which includes the US, stood "in full solidarity with Germany".

Russia has rejected German accusations that a drone carrying explosives deliberately targeted a Ukrainian cargo plane on 4 August.

The drone was defused by a robot at Leipzig/Halle airport and a second drone is thought to have collided with another cargo plane.

A third drone was reportedly found 10 days later at the airport, which is an important Nato hub and is regularly used by Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft.

It was not until Tuesday that the German government said police investigations and intelligence finding had proved that Russia was behind the incidents.

The interior minister said that the drone's configuration, components, explosives and detonator were all known from other Russian hybrid operations.

Two suspects have reportedly been identified in the Leipzig attack, including a Belarusian with a Russian passport who entered on a tourist visa, and another with Latvian and Russian passports who arrived by plane in Berlin and flew out two days before the failed attack.

Berlin has said it will close the Russian consulate in Bonn as well as the Russian House cultural institution, widely suspected in Berlin of acting as a propaganda outlet for the Kremlin.

The Russian foreign ministry promised to respond in "mirror-image" fashion and said Berlin had offered no evidence to back its claims. Germany's chargé d'affaires Bernd Finke was summoned to hear Moscow's rejection of Berlin's "entirely unfounded accusations".

Vladimir Putin has condemned Germany's measures as a serious mistake that "clearly runs counter to the interests of the German people".

Asked whether Moscow would be prepared to sever relations with Berlin, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko answered "maybe", but said for now it was giving diplomacy a chance.

Critics in Germany suggested the German response was relatively weak, but Berlin has its eye on a more co-ordinated response with its allies, including extended EU sanctions and entry restrictions on Russian visitors across the bloc.

Rosenberg: Putin's veiled threat to UK part of Russia's campaign against West

Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack

Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations

Von der Leyen was clear in her statement that the Leipzig attack had involved "military-grade material carried out by Russian operatives on European Union soil".

While she was meeting Rutte in Brussels, EU foreign ministers had gathered at Wicklow in Ireland, where France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said action could be taken on a European level against Russia's so-called "shadow fleet" of ships carrying oil and other cargo aimed at avoiding EU sanctions.

Barrot and fellow ministers from Belgium and the Netherlands said they had summoned Russian ambassadors in protest at the attack.

Lithuania's Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said it was obvious that Russia saw no political cost in its hybrid operations against European allies.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said they were working on how to tighten enforcement of existing sanctions, and added there was broad support for an EU visa entry ban on Russian ex-combatants as well as stricter visa limits on Russian tourists.

Several EU countries, including Sweden, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain, are pushing for more than €193bn (£165bn) in frozen Russian assets to be used to help Ukraine. The idea was first planned at the end of 2025, and rejected by Belgium where the money is held. However, Belgium's position is unchanged because it fears being held financially liable by the courts.

The Leipzig attack was part of a broader pattern of increasingly dangerous incidents, including drones and interference with critical infrastructure, von der Leyen said.

Mark Rutte added there had been increased risk to Europeans from drones and missiles crossing into countries on the Alliance's eastern flank, and there had been more "malign activities targeting our territory directly, whether it is fires set in factories producing defence equipment for Ukraine or indeed the Russian hybrid attack in Leipzig".

Several acts of suspected sabotage have been reported in Germany in the past 24 hours alone, including two attacks on electricity substations, one in the east and one in the west near Cologne.

Although authorities do not yet know who was behind the incidents, North Rhine-Westphalia Interior Minister Herbert Reul said an attack that targeted power lines at Bergheim in western Germany was deliberate and whoever had carried out was attacking the country as a whole.

"We are investigating two possibilities: sabotage directed by a foreign state and left-wing extremism," he said.

Several power lines failed prompting five power plant units to go offline at two separate coal-fired power stations. Police said six launching devices had been found in a field.

High-voltage power lines were damaged near the Jänschwalde coal-fired power plant in Brandenburg early on Tuesday and explosive devices were later found at a substation.

Meanwhile, in neighbouring Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a fire at a factory producing combat drones at Skarżysko-Kamienna, 140km (85 miles) south of Warsaw was a deliberate act of arson and sabotage. Arson has also not been ruled out in a fire at a factory in Lublin on Sunday night.

Von der Leyen said sanctions had already been used to deter Russia, and EU foreign ministers were discussing further ways of "cutting deeper in Russia's war chest".

The EU has already agreed to loan Ukraine €90bn (£77bn), and von der Leyen said Kyiv had asked for billions of extra euros in funding to help pay for PAC-3 air defence missiles. Work was already taking place on a joint Europe-Ukraine Freyja anti-ballistic missile defence project, she added.

She promised that Europe and Nato would just maintain pressure on Moscow but "we will increase it and we will not stop, not until Russia stops bombing and killing innocent children, men and children in Ukraine".

articles.title: Trump: ‘When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?’
articles.summary: President Trump on Tuesday questioned when the Iranian people would “rise up and fight,” as he dismissed the notion the U.S. was trying to pressure Tehran to renew negotiations as the war enters its seventh month. Trump noted that he “couldn’t care less” whether Iran signs an agreement with the U.S. or not. “I’m not…
articles.body:
President Trump on Tuesday questioned when the Iranian people would “rise up and fight,” as he dismissed the notion the U.S. was trying to pressure Tehran to renew negotiations as the war enters its seventh month.

Trump noted that he “couldn’t care less” whether Iran signs an agreement with the U.S. or not.

“I’m not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table, as ABC Fake News reported,” the president wrote on Truth Social . “I couldn’t care less if they sign a worthless, to them, agreement.”

He appeared to be responding to a report from ABC News chief White House correspondent Mary Bruce that said the administration was looking to ramp up economic pressure on Iran. The report cited Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent telling Fox Business in a recent interview that the U.S. would “economically asphyxiate Iran and force them to the bargaining table.”

Bessent has repeatedly tied the administration’s economic campaign against Iran to bringing the country back to talks after a signed memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran failed.

On Monday, he suggested Iran’s economy could collapse “ within weeks or months ,” though he added that a full collapse would not be necessary if Iranian leaders “come to their senses.”

The Treasury Department chief also threatened additional sanctions against Iranian banks and warned that countries and financial institutions that continue to do business with the Islamic Republic could face consequences.

Trump, however, said Tuesday evening that he prefers the U.S.’s current position and doubled down on previous statements that reaching an agreement with the regime was not a priority.

“I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing,” he wrote. “They are just playing out the inevitable.”

“When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?” the president added.

U.S. forces launched a new round of strikes at Iran on Tuesday, targeting its air defenses and other military assets. The strikes were in response to Iranian attacks on U.S. military assets in Jordan and on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz .

Trump warned Tehran earlier Tuesday that if Iran retaliated, it would be hit at a “much harder and higher level.”

Iran nevertheless fired missiles and drones at U.S. military assets across the Middle East early Wednesday, including in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq.

articles.title: Clooney rips Hegseth’s post knocking Canadian military: ‘What’s wrong with you?’
articles.summary: George Clooney is ripping Pete Hegseth and questioning his “sense of decency” after the Defense secretary appeared to poke fun at Canada’s military in a social media post. “You see what the secretary of Defense just tweeted out a picture about women from the military in Canada, and you’re going, ‘What’s wrong with you?’” Clooney…
articles.body:
George Clooney is ripping Pete Hegseth and questioning his “sense of decency” after the Defense secretary appeared to poke fun at Canada’s military in a social media post.

“You see what the secretary of Defense just tweeted out a picture about women from the military in Canada, and you’re going, ‘What’s wrong with you?'” Clooney told reporters in remarks at the Venice Film Festival on Wednesday, where the “Good Night, and Good Luck” star was being honored with the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement.

“Where’s the sense of decency in all of this?” Clooney asked.

The 65-year-old actor’s comments came after Hegseth on Monday posted a photo and caption on the social platform X seemingly mocking the physical appearance of some of the Canadian military’s cadets.

Hegseth’s post featured a screenshot of an Instagram post from a branch of Canada’s Cadet Program that highlighted some recipients of awards in the Canadian military’s youth program.

“(this is real),” Hegseth posted, along with an emoji of a Canadian flag. The message came amid a trade dispute and heightened tensions between the U.S. and Canada.

Referring to Hegseth’s post, Clooney said, “I’m ashamed of all that.”

“The idea that cruelty is the base — that being cruel and unkind is part of the fun of all of this,” he said.

“But we will get through it, and we will come out better on the other side,” Clooney said.

Asked by a journalist how he views the U.S., Clooney replied, “I’m always very optimistic about things, and I do believe that … we’re at a moment in time that’s unfortunate — I think that’s a understatement. I do believe that we’re going to get through all of this.”

“I’m old enough to have been through 1968 in the states, when every city in the United States was set on fire, and we lost Martin Luther King and Bobby Kennedy. The same year, there was tons of violence. The capital was surrounded with tanks,” the Academy Award winner said.

“We’ve had some other difficult times, but this is one of them,” Clooney said.

“There’s a great word: kakistocracy, which is a country run by the least qualified people,” continued Clooney, a critic of President Trump and a top Hollywood fundraiser for Democrats.

“I think maybe we have a kakistocracy right now, but we’ll get through it,” he said.

Clooney, who in a 2024 New York Times op-ed called on then-President Biden to drop out of that year’s White House race on account of age-related concerns, expressed optimism about the next midterm and presidential elections.

“We will have an election in November that should be a check and balance,” he said.

“And then in 2028, with any luck, we’ll have some restoration into some normalcy.”

articles.title: Nepal PM 'thanks' India, China for aid after minister seeks 'compensation' for deadly flood
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Wednesday thanked India and China for their swift assistance after devastating flash floods killed over 1,000 pe.
articles.body: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Wednesday thanked India and China for their swift assistance after devastating flash floods killed over 1,000 people and left nearly 4,900 missing.Addressing the House of Representatives, Shah said the government had been coordinating with the international community from the beginning and had sought to expedite procedures to receive assistance.Teams from India and China expressed interest in helping soon after the disaster, he said, according to The Kathmandu Post.Foreign teams initially conducted aerial assessments but were unable to land because of difficult ground conditions. They later reached the affected areas once helicopters could operate safely and heavy equipment could be deployed, he added.India has provided both relief supplies and specialised assistance to Nepal. New Delhi sent the fifth tranche of relief material on Tuesday, with an Indian Air Force aircraft carrying an 11-member rescue team, specialised equipment and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines.“The fifth Indian aircraft has departed for Nepal. It is carrying an 11-member rescue team with specialised equipment, and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines,” external affairs minister S Jaishankar said in a post on X on Tuesday.Indian teams have also been assisting with search and rescue operations around hydropower tunnels and supporting forensic work to identify victims amid the large number of casualties and missing people.Shah also claimed that the scale of the disaster had raised serious questions about the growing risks faced by people in the Himalayan region because of climate change.“According to experts, the flash flood in Bhotekoshi of Rasuwa district was caused by an ice-rock avalanche in the Himalayas. This incident shows the increasing risk the people of the mountain region have to bear with the occurrence of climate change,” he said.“Therefore,” Shah stressed, “We need to present the fact in a strong manner to the international community that the disaster is linked to climate change.”“There is a global contribution behind climate change. And the responsibility to manage and minimise its effects also rests with the global community,” the prime minister added.Nepal minister seeks compensation from IndiaEarlier in the day, foreign minister Shisir Khanal called for greater international accountability, saying Nepal contributes “virtually negligible” greenhouse gas emissions but is bearing a disproportionate share of the consequences of climate change.“We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create. The rapid melting of glaciers and these catastrophic mountain tsunamis are direct consequences of global climate change,” Khanal said in an interview with Kantipur TV, excerpts of which were published by The Kathmandu Post.Khanal said Nepal was shifting its diplomatic approach from seeking “aid” to demanding “justice and compensation”.“This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability,” he said, adding that Nepal would raise the issue “with absolute firmness and clarity” at international forums.According to news agency PTI, Khanal identified China, the US and India as the world’s three largest greenhouse gas emitters and said they had a “historical responsibility to compensate vulnerable nations like Nepal”.“This is a matter of civilisational survival. If our Himalayan glaciers disappear, the water security of over two billion people in South Asia dependent on rivers like the Ganges and the Trishuli will be permanently compromised. We are advocating not just for Nepal, but for the survival of South Asian civilisation,” he said.Nepal has formally approached the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, seeking urgent financial assistance following the Bhotekoshi River basin flash flood.A letter jointly signed by finance minister Swarnim Wagle and forests and agriculture minister Geeta Chaudhary said the disaster had caused extensive economic and non-economic losses beyond Nepal’s immediate response capacity.The death toll from the devastating flash floods rose to 1,127 on Wednesday, with nearly 4,900 people still missing, as rescue teams battled continuing rain and debris. The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages across northern and central Nepal.According to Nepal Police, 348 bodies were recovered from Chitwan, 217 from Nawalparasi East, 190 from Nawalparasi West and 155 from Nuwakot. Another 66 bodies were recovered from Gorkha, 59 from Dhading, 45 from Rasuwa and 38 from Tanahu.Police said postmortem and legal identification procedures had been completed for 1,113 bodies, while 95 bodies had been handed over to relatives. Details of 911 unidentified bodies have been uploaded on the Nepal Police website to help families identify missing relatives.Security forces have rescued 6,541 people from affected areas, while search operations continue for 4,858 people reported missing, police said.Authorities have deployed 7,912 police personnel for search and rescue operations, relief distribution and management of recovered bodies.Rescue teams are also relocating families from high-risk areas, clearing debris from roads and coordinating relief operations with local authorities and residents. However, continuing rain has disrupted search and rescue efforts in Rasuwa and Nuwakot.Earlier on Wednesday, health minister Nisha Mehta said India was assisting Nepal in managing the bodies of those killed in the floods, including through DNA testing and support for establishing a laboratory for DNA management.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
