articles.title: How Trumpism is changing the world
articles.summary: This US presidency is rewriting the rules of global governance and ushering the world into a new era.
articles.body:
The post-World War II era was dominated by idealism that gave birth to a dense architecture of multilateral institutions and Western-led governance frameworks.

That order has now reached a decisive historical inflection point. The foreign policy paradigm forged during the two administrations of United States President Donald Trump — marked by unilateralism, transactional nationalism, and a recalibration of historic alliances — represents a sharp break from prior international norms. Combining coercive leverage with strategic media manipulation, this shift has heralded a new foreign policy phenomenon: Trumpism.

By combining assertions of national sovereignty with an anti-establishment tone, Trumpism systematically challenges the core assumptions that had underpinned global governance for generations.

At its core, it represents a deliberate move away from grand, Western-dominated global leadership towards a decentralised, issue-specific, and deeply transactional international order.

Trumpism’s operational strategy has replaced traditional multilateral commitments with a hardheaded focus on economic statecraft and national interest. Foreign policy engagements have been explicitly tethered to domestic economic priorities: reindustrialisation, a revitalised defence industrial base, energy dominance, balanced trade, and leadership in the financial sector.

To achieve these aims, the Trump administration has eschewed expansive multinational agreements in favour of bilateral bargains, deploying aggressive tariffs, coercive trade measures, and sanctions as primary instruments of state power.

The administration’s reliance on expansive sanctions regimes and aggressive extraterritorial enforcement has ignited fierce global debates regarding international law, state sovereignty, and the legitimate limits of national jurisdiction.

Under the banner of “peace through strength”, Trumpism has integrated legal, economic, and security mechanisms to pressure allies and adversaries alike. Law enforcement operations and national security objectives have been routinely repurposed as direct tools of foreign policy.

This transactional posture has extended directly into collective defence and security architectures, most notably NATO. Trumpism has brought intense scrutiny to Western defence burden-sharing arrangements, highlighting severe imbalances where the US had borne a disproportionate share of costs and strategic risks.

Institutional disruption and systemic paralysis

The systemic consequences of Trumpism have reverberated across every layer of the global governance hierarchy.

In multilateral forums, the administration has displayed unprecedented ambivalence and unpredictability, frequently reneging on established international agreements and disengaging from multilateral institutions.

This volatile leadership style has exposed deep vulnerabilities within global governance, accelerating the fragmentation of the post-Cold War liberal international order.

A prominent casualty of this institutional disruption has been the United Nations, particularly the UN Security Council. Trump’s policies have magnified existing debates over the UNSC’s legitimacy, representation, and effectiveness.

Observers have noted that entrenched geopolitical rivalries, institutional inertia, and structural hierarchies rooted in the colonial era had already left the UNSC paralysed—trapped in a pre-contemplation stage of reform rather than delivering substantive structural changes. US institutional disengagement has further compounded this inertia, raising fundamental questions about the long-term durability and authority of international security bodies.

While proponents have argued that the Trump administration is seeking to drive necessary institutional reform through selective, high-level engagement—such as collaborating with like-minded allies and engaging the UN secretary-general on shared priorities—critics have viewed these moves as prioritising immediate national interests over global stability.

The rise of a multipolar and regionalised order

As the US is stepping back from global stewardship, the resulting power vacuum is catalysing a profound restructuring of international politics. Middle powers and regional blocs are increasingly stepping forward to bridge governance gaps.

These actors have begun constructing regional frameworks and issue-specific coalitions, casting them as vital supplements — or direct alternatives — to traditional Western-dominated institutions.

This global pivot has ignited a fierce debate among international relations scholars and policymakers regarding Trump’s legacy.

On the one hand, some argue that the disruptions he has caused are a catalyst for reform and systemic resilience. By forcing middle powers and non-Western nations to take greater ownership of regional security and economic coordination, Trumpism is fostering a more plural, inclusive, and realistic global order capable of addressing modern geopolitical realities.

Others are warning that US disengagement from multilateral commitments has shattered collective security arrangements and degraded institutional legitimacy. From this viewpoint, weakened Western leadership has paved the way for sustained strategic competition, regional instability, and dangerous governance voids across critical international forums.

The foreign policy of the Trump presidency cannot be dismissed as a temporary aberration or a simple shift in personal political style; it warrants the enduring label Trumpism because it has established a distinct, reproducible paradigm of international statecraft.

By deliberately weaponising unpredictable diplomacy, prioritising national prosperity over institutional continuity, and asserting absolute national sovereignty against global governance constraints, Trumpism fundamentally is redefining how a great power can exercise leverage in the modern era.

Trump’s foreign policy will leave an indelible imprint on the contemporary international system. By challenging the foundational premises of the liberal international order, it will permanently alter the balance of power, forcing the world into a new era characterised by decentralised authority, heightened regionalism, and a continuous search for new governance models.

articles.title: A former eBay CEO bought a 1,530-acre California fishing ranch for $12.6 million; seven years later, she sold it for $17.9 million
articles.summary: US News: Meg Whitman, the former chief executive of eBay, has sold her vast California fishing ranch for $17.9 million, marking the latest chapter in the histo.
articles.body: Meg Whitman, the former chief executive of eBay, has sold her vast California fishing ranch for $17.9 million, marking the latest chapter in the history of a property that she and her husband bought seven years earlier for about $12.6 million. The 1,530-acre ‘Spring Creek Ranch’ sits in the Fall River Valley, roughly 230 miles north of Sacramento, combining extensive open land with private access to renowned fishing waters. Whitman and her husband, neurosurgeon Dr Griff Harsh, acquired the property in 2019 before moving to Telluride, Colorado. According to Realtor, the ranch went on the market in April 2026 at $18.5 million and found a buyer within around two months. The sale brings an end to Whitman’s ownership of one of Northern California’s distinctive recreational estates and places the property in the hands of a new owner with a strong personal connection to fly fishing.Meg Whitman’s 1,530-acre California fishing ranch finds a new ownerSpring Creek Ranch is known for combining substantial acreage with access to the Fall River and its surrounding waters. According to Realtor, the estate includes private fishing opportunities, a main residence, a barn and several outbuildings. Spring Creek, one of the important headwaters connected to the Fall River system, runs through the property. The ranch is located in the rural Fall River Valley, where the landscape and waterways have long been central to the area's appeal. Another distinctive feature is a custom ‘Airstream fishing camp,’ added by a previous owner. These features helped set the property apart from a conventional country estate, offering a combination of residential accommodation and outdoor recreation. The buyer was California investor ‘Kelly J. Barlow,’ who purchased the ranch through a limited liability company, according to Realtor.The sale ends a seven-year chapter for Whitman and her husbandWhitman and her husband, Dr Griff Harsh, purchased Spring Creek Ranch for approximately $12.6 million in 2019. According to Realtor, the couple later expanded their connection to the area. In 2023, they paid a further $3 million for 57 acres of nearby land. By that point, however, they had already moved to Telluride, Colorado, where they relocated in 2020. Spring Creek Ranch was listed for sale in April 2026 at $18.5 million. According to Realtor, the property sold about two months later for $17.9 million. The transaction closed a period of ownership that had begun with the couple's purchase of the original property seven years earlier.Why was the ranch’s private fishing access so valuableWhile the size of the property was significant, its access to private fishing was one of its strongest attractions. According to Realtor, Todd Renfrew, who represented the buyer, said that the ranch's private fishing opportunities made it particularly appealing. For buyers interested in recreational land, direct access to fishing waters can be a defining feature. That appeal also appears to align closely with the interests of the new owner. Barlow is an avid fly fisherman and serves as the board chair of ‘California Trout,’ a conservation nonprofit. The buyer's background gives the sale an especially fitting outcome. Rather than simply acquiring a large rural estate, Barlow purchased a property whose defining features include the outdoor activity in which he is personally involved.California’s high-value ranch market continues to attract buyersThe Spring Creek Ranch sale also reflects the continued demand for distinctive recreational properties in California. According to Realtor, interest in ranch properties increased during the Covid-19 pandemic as some buyers looked for more space away from major cities. Renfrew said the market had remained ‘pretty steady,’ with properties continuing to change hands. Ranches such as Spring Creek occupy a specialised part of the property market. Their value can depend on a combination of location, land size, natural features and recreational opportunities rather than on the house alone. This sale underlines the lasting appeal of rare rural properties that offer a combination of privacy, extensive land and direct access to natural features. Spring Creek Ranch may have changed hands, but the qualities that made it distinctive remain central to its value.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: China’s Xi visits Egypt’s el-Sisi: Why it matters
articles.summary: Xi Jinping’s historic Egypt visit aims to strengthen China-Egypt ties amid rising Middle East tensions.
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting Egypt for the first time in a decade, as Cairo looks to foster deeper economic and military ties with Beijing while maintaining its long-standing relationship with Washington.

The visit comes as the US-Israel war on Iran and resulting disruption to global trade have prompted US allies in the region to reassess their strategic relationships. Most recently, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye announced the Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement , a mutual defence pact.

Seeking closer ties with Beijing, therefore, is part of an effort to further what President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has called Cairo’s “independent foreign policy”.

For China, Egypt offers an important foothold in the Middle East with its large economy, control of the Suez Canal and diplomatic influence across the Arab world and Africa.

Xi’s three-day visit, which began on Tuesday evening, includes talks with el-Sisi that are expected to focus on the regional conflict and its consequences for maritime trade security, as well as expanding Chinese investment in Egypt.

The two countries are expected to sign economic agreements covering areas including artificial intelligence (AI), transport and manufacturing.

The visit marks 70 years of diplomatic relations between Egypt and China. Egyptian state-run media reported that Xi has called for the two countries to “expand the scope of pragmatic collaboration”, while el-Sisi praised Chinese investment in Egypt and reiterated Cairo’s support for Beijing’s position on Taiwan, the island nation that China claims as part of its own territory.

Military cooperation is another increasingly important part of the relationship.

In August, Egypt and China held joint air exercises including Chinese J-16 fighter jets and Egypt’s French-made Rafale aircraft. It was the first time the J-16s had taken part in a combat exercise alongside the Rafales.

Xi’s visit highlights Beijing’s efforts to expand its influence in a region where the US has been the dominant military power for decades.

Egypt is a key Middle East ally for Washington, and the second-largest recipient of US military aid.

The meeting comes at a time of considerable geopolitical instability, with Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the US-Israel war with Iran, and disruption around the Red Sea caused by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis targeting Saudi-linked ships all raising questions about the durability of the existing US-led regional order, experts say.

Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer in international security at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera, “China is trying to position itself as an increasingly important economic and diplomatic actor in that environment, particularly as a counterweight to the US, as a more responsible and more hands-off regional actor.”

Egypt has a population of 110 million and is an important market for Chinese goods and investment. It is also particularly important to Beijing because it controls the Suez Canal, Pinfold said, adding that the waterway has become even more critical amid disruptions to shipping in the crucial Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz straits.

Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz for the past six months in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes. Prior to the war, more than one-fifth of the world’s oil and petroleum products were shipped through the strait, which is the only sea route to the open ocean available to Gulf producers.

China offers Egypt opportunities to develop investment, infrastructure and technology, while bilateral ties have also expanded into areas including defence and artificial intelligence.

But the growing relationship should not be interpreted as Egypt pivoting away from the US entirely, Pinfold said, noting that “instead, el-Sisi’s approach is better understood as one of diversification and strategic autonomy”.

“In short,” Pinfold said, “as the Gulf states have done in recent years, he is trying to hedge without alienating or annoying Egypt’s indisputably most important ally, the US.”

Relations between Cairo and Beijing have deepened significantly since 2014, when el-Sisi visited China and the two countries signed a strategic partnership agreement.

China is now Egypt’s largest trading partner in non-petroleum goods, with bilateral trade reaching nearly $20.7bn by the end of 2025, according to Egypt’s State Information Service (SIS).

Data from the country’s Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) shows a nearly 200 percent increase in Egyptian exports to China, at $840.8m in the first half of 2026, while imports stood at $10.4bn.

Beijing has also invested more than $10bn in Egypt, including in the New Administrative Capital east of Cairo and an electric rail line serving industry in the Nile Delta.

Chinese companies have also invested in container ports, green hydrogen, iron pipes, tyres and satellites.

Chinese investments in Egypt are focused mainly in the Suez Canal area and the China-Egypt TEDA cooperation zone in Ain Sokhna, part of Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative, which hosts about 200 companies with investments exceeding $3.8bn, according to Egyptian state media.

In 2023, Egypt joined BRICS, the bloc of Global South nations including Brazil, Russia, India and China.

articles.title: Cuisinart Grill Brush Recall Expands to 3.6 Million Units — Shop Safe Alternatives
articles.summary: The CPSC says 3.6 million Cuisinart wire grill brushes are now recalled over an ingestion hazard. Here’s what to do if you have one, plus safer alternatives to shop before Labor Day.
articles.body: With Labor Day weekend marking one of the last big grilling occasions of the summer, it’s worth double-checking what’s in your grilling toolkit. The United States Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) has just expanded its recall of Cuisinart grill brushes, bringing the total number of affected units to 3.6 million. The original recall in July covered 1.7 million brushes, and last Thursday regulators added another 1.9 million to the list, citing risks that loose bristles could break off, embed in food and cause injury if swallowed. Below, find the full recall details, plus some safer grill brush alternatives you can shop right now, including many that will arrive before you fire up your barbecue for the holiday weekend. Why were Cuisinart grill brushes recalled? Conair, which makes Cuisinart-branded grill tools, first recalled 1.7 million wire bristle grill brushes in July 2026. That recall has now been expanded to include another 1.9 million brushes, bringing the total to about 3,625,800 recalled units. The recall covers brushes sold between June 2009 through March 2026, including models sold on their own as well as ones bundled inside larger grill-tool sets. The brushes were sold at Walmart, Burlington, TJ Maxx and Ross, along with online retailers including Amazon and Cuisinart’s website. There are more than 20 models that have been recalled, but what you really need to know is that the recall now encompasses all wired grill brushes made by Cuisinart. Translation: If you have a wired grill brush from this brand, it’s part of the recall. The danger, according to the CPSC, is that small metal wire bristles can detach from the brushes and stick to the grill or food, creating an ingestion hazard that could lead to serious internal injuries requiring surgery. The CPSC reports that Conair is aware of at least 54 reports of bristles detaching, including three cases in which people swallowed metal bristles and needed medical treatment to remove them from their throat or digestive tract. Anyone with one of the affected brushes is being told to stop using it immediately. What to do if you have a recalled Cuisinart grill brush It’s worth repeating: If you have one of the recalled brushes, stop using it right away. You’ll need to discard the brush; there’s no repair option being offered here. From there, you can contact Conair to get a refund. You can reach the company toll-free at 888-520-1304, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. ET, or you can file for a refund online at recallrtr.com/grillbrushes or through Cuisinart.com under “Product Recalls.” Consumers have two options when it comes to refunds: a straightforward cash refund, or a credit to use at Cuisinart.com worth the refund amount plus an extra 20 percent. Wire grill brush alternatives you can shop right now This isn’t the first time we’ve flagged the risks that come with wire grill brushes — we’ve previously reported on the dangers of stray bristles and gathered advice from experts on safer ways to clean your grill. The alternatives below adhere to that guidance, and each one carries at least a four-star average rating from hundreds of shoppers. This GrillArt grill brush is made with a proprietary flexible woven steel fiber head to clean stuck on food from the grill. It’s most effective with steam, so all you need to do is turn on your grill (then turn it off), dip the brush in water and let the heat and porous fibers get to work. The long 16.5-inch handle also means you never have to get directly up on the heated cooker while you clean it. This bristle-free brush uses durable, heat-resistant fiber to scrub away grate residue, with a replaceable, square-shaped head that doubles as a scraper for flat-top grills. The 14-inch handle keeps your hand away from the heat, and compatible accessories, like a bottle opener, can attach to it. Just dip it in water and scrape — it uses steam instead of metal bristles to clean and it works even while the grill is still hot. This brush also skips bristles altogether, relying instead on interlocking stainless steel coils (think chainmail) to scrub grates clean. My husband and I grill weekly in the summer and this is his favorite tool — and that is saying a lot because he has tested a ton of different grill brushes. The head comes off with ease when it needs to be replaced or cleaned, and it can go straight into the dishwasher along with the heat-resistant handle. It also works whether your grill is hot or has already cooled down. A woven stainless steel head does the scrubbing on this cleaner — no loose wires involved. Crank your grill to 400 degrees or higher then turn it off, dunk the brush in water, then go over the grates while they’re still hot — steam does the heavy lifting, loosening gunk without giving your arm a workout. Five dishwasher-safe replacement heads come in the box, along with a steel scraper built in for stubborn spots. Why trust NBC Selected? articles.title: In 1941, US Steel built a summer camp lodge at Indiana Dunes; after about 50 years closed, it has reopened and workers found an original time capsule hidden in its walls
articles.summary: US News: Generations of Northwest Indiana children began their adventure at a summer camp along the Little Calumet River. Almost a century after the lodge open.
articles.body: Generations of Northwest Indiana children began their adventure at a summer camp along the Little Calumet River. Almost a century after the lodge opened its doors, the historic building at Indiana Dunes National Park is once again open for visitors. The reopening has an unexpected link to the past, thanks to a long-forgotten time capsule found hidden within its walls, states a National Park Service report. The Good Fellow Camp Lodge has been significantly rehabilitated, starting a new chapter for a building that was once the hub of a summer camp for thousands of children. According to the report, in 1941, the U.S. Steel Company built the lodge for the children of its employees. The Good Fellow Youth Camp, which ran from 1941 to 1975, provided generations of young people with an opportunity to get outdoors in what would later become Indiana Dunes National Park. The camp’s distinctive architecture and history also speak to the industrial heritage of Northwest Indiana, where the steel industry was a major force in shaping local communities. The camp was closed and the lodge sat vacant for decades. The restoration today allows the historic structure to once again serve the public.A time capsule buried in the wallsWhile renovating, workers discovered something incredible: an original time capsule hidden inside the building from when it was constructed. The capsule was on display during the ceremonial reopening, serving as a physical connection to the lodge’s earliest history for former campers and other visitors. The park intends to restore the capsule inside the lodge, adding more items that reflect the building and its community today, rather than simply returning the capsule to where it was hidden. The end result will be a physical connection between those who built and enjoyed the lodge decades ago, and the guests who will enjoy it in the future.Campers are backAlumni of the Good Fellow Youth Camp returned for the reopening and reminisced about the history of the building and its role in their childhood. Partners in the ceremony included the National Park Foundation, Save the Dunes, Friends of Indiana Dunes and the Dunes Learning Center. The restored lodge will offer educational programs and community events and give visitors another way to experience the park’s history.A component of broader preservation effortsThe rehabilitation is part of a $25.4 million project to restore historic structures throughout Indiana Dunes National Park. Funding for the lodge was through the Legacy Restoration Fund established by the Great American Outdoors Act of 2020. The program is assisting the National Park Service with long-delayed maintenance and boosting the safety, reliability and accessibility of historic public structures. Other Indiana Dunes projects funded by the fund include preservation work at the Bailly Homestead, an early 19th-century national historic landmark, and the House of Tomorrow, the futuristic home created for the 1933 Chicago World's Fair.Linking the past and the futureToday, Indiana Dunes National Park has more than 50 miles of trails through forests, wetlands, shifting dunes and the Lake Michigan shoreline. The restored lodge adds another layer to that experience, preserving a piece of the region’s industrial and recreational history while making room for future generations. The park's economic impact extends far beyond its borders. In 2024, visitors added an estimated $143 million to the local economy, demonstrating the park’s importance to Northwest Indiana.Image Courtesy: Lakeshore Public MediaCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Four arrested over Anglesey murder of Doreen Morris 32 years ago
articles.summary: Police said advances in forensic science and a review of evidence had led to the development.
articles.body:
Four people have been arrested on suspicion of perverting the course of justice in the case of a woman who was murdered 32 years ago.

Doreen Morris, 64, was stabbed to death with a fork after disturbing a burglary at her home, Penrhyn Uchaf, on Anglesey, in 1994, according to a 2023 inquest .

Joseph Carl Westbury denied breaking into Doreen's bungalow and was found not guilty of her murder in 1995. He took his life in May 2016.

North Wales Police said a man and three women, all from north Wales, were arrested on Wednesday morning.

The force said advances in forensic science and a review of evidence had led to the development and the Morris family had been told.

Mark Pierce, senior review officer, said: "Forensic results, combined with a detailed review of witness evidence, have provided grounds to interview four people on suspicion of perverting the course of justice."

He appealed for anyone with information about the case to get in touch.

articles.title: China’s Xi urges new Middle East security framework during rare Egypt visit
articles.summary: Chinese, Egyptian leaders discuss the US-Israel war on Iran, which has prompted regional powers to rethink defence.
articles.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has called on Middle East countries to oppose external influence and consider reshaping the region’s security order.

Xi’s remarks on Wednesday to his Egyptian counterpart Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, on his first visit to Cairo in a decade, come as Beijing seeks to expand its influence in the region amid the United States-Israel war with Iran .

“We must uphold the principle that the people of the Middle East are the masters of their own affairs, oppose external interference [and] support regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security,” Xi said in a meeting with el-Sisi, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

Xi was greeted by el-Sisi and a 21-gun salute for talks at the Ittihadiya presidential palace in the Egyptian capital.

The talks covered the six-month US-Israel war on Iran, with both presidents urging “diplomatic solutions” to reach a “comprehensive agreement to end the war”, according to a statement from el-Sisi’s spokesperson.

Sisi’s office also said the two countries signed an agreement to launch the third phase of the Egyptian-Chinese industrial zone at the Suez Canal, which officials say already hosts 200 companies and investments worth approximately $4bn.

The new investments – for which Egypt has not announced a figure – give Beijing even greater influence in the canal zone, a critical artery of global trade, as conflict in the region chokes traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, which passes between Oman and Iran, and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, which separates Yemen and the Horn of Africa.

Xi said China “stands ready to work with countries in the region to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation … and eliminate the breeding grounds for conflict”.

A series of additional agreements were also signed, though Egyptian officials did not provide details.

Beijing is eyeing a greater foothold in the Middle East, at a time when “the United States looks like it can’t really make up its mind whether it wants to withdraw from the region or be more engaged”, Mirette Mabrouk, a senior fellow at the Washington-based Middle East Institute, told the AFP news agency.

China sees Egypt as a key partner and an entry point to more regional influence. For Egypt, closer ties with China are part of a broader effort to diversify partnerships rather than align with a single power, Mabrouk said.

The diplomatic campaign comes before an expected meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump this month.

Cairo is one of the largest recipients of US military aid, receiving $1.3bn annually, and has historically served as a key Middle East mediator.

Xi’s visit also comes after Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan last month signed the Mecca Defence Alliance. Experts have said the move demonstrates a desire by regional countries to diversify their security arrangements beyond Washington.

The US-Israel war with Iran has led several regional allies to question the dependability of the traditional US security guarantee. Washington has, in turn, called on Gulf partners to take greater charge of their own regional deterrence.

The pact contains a NATO-style Article 5 clause , meaning an armed attack on any of the three member states is considered an attack on all.

Officials in Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have stressed the pact is not meant to replace any pre-existing security deals.

Across Cairo, a megalopolis home to more than 26 million people, major streets were lined on Wednesday with Chinese and Egyptian flags, as well as billboards showing el-Sisi and Xi.

Xi is expected to head to the Grand Egyptian Museum overlooking the Giza Pyramids later on Wednesday.

articles.title: Mamdani expected to announce AI ban in NYC schools for young students
articles.summary: When New York City schools resume next week, a new restriction on the use of artificial intelligence will reportedly be in place for students and teachers.
articles.body: When New York City schools resume next week, a new restriction on the use of artificial intelligence will reportedly be in place for students and teachers. The New York Times reports that a policy scheduled to be announced Wednesday would put an age restriction on students who get to use AI, in addition to individual screen time. The announcement is expected to be made by Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels later this morning. Under the plan, New York City public schools would impose a one-year pause on students using AI until they get to high school — that accounts for nearly 600,000 young leaners. The mandate would also place restrictions on the use of devices like laptops and tablets, with students from preschool through 2nd grade not being allowed to use them in class. Students in 3rd grade to 8th grade will reportedly have time limits on using laptops. These new rules on technology in the classroom come as the mayor has been quoted as pushing back on the use of AI in schools, saying despite the push from the tech industry, AI-powered early education is not inevitable. Leaders in the Department of Education have reportedly spent months putting together a guidebook on AI in the classroom that includes feedback from lawmakers, tech companies and parents. The schools chancellor has previously said the guardrails would protect the “human connection, curiosity and creativity that help children grow.” Teachers in the city, however, will not have the same restrictions. Under the new policy, they will still be able to use artificial intelligence for things like creating lesson plans but they won’t be allowed to use the tool for grading or crisis management. The AI policies in New York City schools are being seen as some of the most restrictive on technology in the classroom nationwide.

articles.title: Dismissal of ex-US soldier Bergdahl’s conviction was invalid, court rules
articles.summary: Appeals panel says only military tribunals may assess court-martial convictions in blow to former Afghan war prisoner.
articles.body:
A federal judge had no authority to overturn former US Army soldier Bowe Bergdahl’s military conviction for deserting his post in Afghanistan before Taliban-allied forces captured him and held him for nearly five years, an appeals court has ruled.

A three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit on Tuesday ordered the dismissal of Bergdahl’s claims in district court. The ruling essentially reinstates the ex-soldier’s conviction.

The panel said District Judge Reggie Walton, sitting in Washington, DC, lacked the jurisdiction to vacate Bergdahl’s court-martial conviction and sentence in 2023.

Bergdahl had sued in civilian court in 2021, arguing that the military punishment violated his Fifth Amendment due-process rights. Walton ruled that military judge Jeffrey Nance created a potential conflict of interest by failing to disclose his application for a position as an immigration judge in the US Department of Justice.

But the appeals court concluded that only a court of appeals within the military justice system has the authority to overturn a court-martial judgement.

“Because Bergdahl seeks to have his court-martial conviction declared expunged and without effect due to violations of the Constitution and military rules, and its consequences reversed, he effectively asked the District Court to vacate the military judgment,” Circuit Judge Robert Wilkins wrote. “However, the authority to vacate a court-martial judgment belongs to tribunals exercising direct appellate review, not district courts conducting collateral review.”

Bergdahl, then a 23-year-old soldier from Hailey, Idaho, was stationed in eastern Afghanistan’s Paktika province in June 2009 when he left his post without permission . His defence team said he left to hike to headquarters to complain about what he viewed as poor leadership in his unit.

Bergdahl was captured by forces from the Taliban-affiliated Haqqani Network and repeatedly tortured before his release from captivity in 2014 as part of a prisoner swap under then-President Barack Obama.

The deal – which freed five Taliban prisoners from the Guantanamo Bay detention facility – was sharply criticised by some conservatives, including Donald Trump, who would be elected president two years later.

In 2015 during his campaign, Trump called for the death penalty for Bergdahl. He also criticised the decision to spare him jail time, calling it a “disgrace” to the country.

Several US service members were wounded during the search for Bergdahl, who was charged with desertion and misbehaviour before the enemy after his release from captivity. He pleaded guilty to both charges in 2017 and was dishonourably discharged. Prosecutors at his court martial had sought 14 years in prison.

articles.title: Bristol scientists may have found first evidence of dark matter
articles.summary: The mysterious material has eluded scientists for nearly a century.
articles.body:
Scientists believe they may be one step closer to detecting dark matter for the first time, but the findings have not been verified by independent researchers.

Scientists from the University of Bristol were part of a two-year study to try and measure the invisible substance thought to make up over 85% of the universe.

Using a sensitive detector in an an underground laboratory in the US, the researchers saw an atom and mystery particle colliding.

Lead researcher physicist Dr Sam Eriksen said it could be "the first step in understanding dark matter as a particle", but further research could also reveal that the particle is not related to dark matter.

"Following a huge amount of scientific effort, this is incredibly exciting," the University of Bristol senior research associate added.

Although scientists have long been certain of the existence of dark matter, because it is invisible as it reflects no light.

While it is thought to make up the majority of mass in the universe, it has never been directly detected.

For two years, 250 scientists and engineers from 39 institutions spanning six countries, including two universities from the UK, have rigorously scrutinised data from one of the world's most sensitive dark matter detectors called LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ).

It is managed by the US Department of Energy's Sanford Underground Research Facility in South Dakota - the deepest laboratory in the US at nearly a mile beneath the ground.

To search for dark matter, LZ uses extremely sensitive light detectors to capture particle interactions.

The study found one particle interaction which could potentially have been caused by a Weakly Interacting Massive Particle, (WIMP), which scientists believe make up dark matter.

But there is currently low statistical evidence in it being a true breakthrough.

The findings were revealed at a conference in Japan on Tuesday, but the research has yet to undergo peer-review by other scientists.

The findings have been rated 2.6 sigma, which is the system that marks the statistical significance of discoveries. The normal threshold is five.

"With only one event, we don't want to get ahead of ourselves," said Professor Rick Gaitskell from Brown University.

"We are not claiming to have seen dark matter. But we have seen something interesting that we want to share with the scientific community for their input."

Professor Henning Flaecher, an experimental particle physicist at the University of Bristol, said a "huge amount" of work had been carried out over "countless hours" to investigate any previously known reasons researchers might have observed the unusual reaction.

"To date none provide a convincing explanation," he said.

"It's an incredibly exciting time, the kind of event every astro-particle physicist dreams of, and we can't wait to analyse more data to see if additional candidate events appear."

articles.title: Isle of Man passport applications to move online
articles.summary: The move to online applications will cut the price to £102 per passport
articles.body:
Applications for Isle of Man passports are set to move online this winter, in one of the biggest changes to the service in years.

The shift means most people will apply through the government website, using a digital system run by His Majesty's Passport Office which already handles millions of UK passport applications each year.

The move is intended to make the process quicker and more convenient, but it also comes with a major change for anyone whose passport is close to expiring.

The most immediate impact for customers is a price drop, with online applications costing £102, down from the current £115.50.

The five‑day Express service will be withdrawn when the online system launches, meaning people relying on a rapid turnaround will need to plan further ahead.

The government said paper forms would still be available for anyone who cannot use the website.

The Passport Office said it understood the change "may present a challenge for some customers", but said support would be offered in the coming month, including help at public workspaces in Douglas.

The update is to bring the island in line with Guernsey and Jersey, due to introduce the same online system at the same time.

Anyone with a passport nearing expiry is being urged to apply in good time, especially once the fast‑track option ends.

articles.title: It’s always Shark Week in Putin’s world. That doesn’t bode well for Trump’s Ukraine peace hopes
articles.summary: When it comes to the war in Ukraine, Putin intends to double down, regardless of where the lines are on the battlefield and whatever economic pain Kyiv manages to inflict on ordinary Russians through a campaign of deep strikes.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin traveled to Kyrgyzstan this week for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit, a regional confab that also brought together Xi Jinping of China, Narendra Modi of India and Masoud Pezeshkian of Iran. The leaders convened in the capital Bishkek during a week of high geopolitical anxiety, with a fresh round of tit-for-tat strikes by Iran and the US, Russian drones and missiles pummeling Ukraine and Germany accusing Russia of being responsible for a drone attack targeting Leipzig airport last month. But Putin appeared firmly in his comfort zone. At a press conference late Tuesday, he seemed to go out of his way to make one point explicit: nations exist in a state of Darwinian competition, and Russia will prevail in a survival-of-the-fittest contest. Asked by Kremlin pool reporter Pavel Zarubin about some unusual remarks he made a few days earlier about killer whales eating polar bears – more on Putin’s views on marine biology in a moment – the Russian president described his statement as a “spontaneous” analogy for Russia’s ongoing confrontation with the West. “I would say that the orca is, without doubt, a formidable predator, yet it is also a highly intelligent creature, a cunning one,” he said. “The collective West, for its part, was assigned a specific definition in the Soviet era, which remains current to this day – the sharks of imperialism.” Sharks and orcas may not quite be the same class of animal, but Putin continued with his analogy. “The thrust of my remarks was that if anyone attempts to drag us down the food chain and devour us, to consume us, they would be well advised to expect their teeth to be broken,” he said. “And Russia stands ready to do precisely that, despite the insatiable appetites and ever-sharpening teeth of these sharks.” The messaging here was clear, both to a domestic audience and to Putin’s international counterparts. When it comes to the war in Ukraine, Putin intends to double down, regardless of where the lines are on the battlefield and whatever economic pain Kyiv manages to inflict on ordinary Russians through a campaign of deep strikes. Putin knows that Ukraine is on the back foot when it comes to defending its skies, and Russian forces have been blanketing Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles. While Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Tuesday that Russian airspace “will effectively be closing” due to the presence of Ukrainian drones, Putin dismissed the escalatory rhetoric, saying he had not heard the remark. Such comments, Putin said, “amount to nothing less than a call for state-sponsored terrorism. And I would point out that they are asking us to resume negotiations and requesting face-to-face meetings. One does not negotiate with terrorists.” Putin was equally dismissive of a claim by Germany that Russia was responsible for a recent drone attack at Leipzig airport, suggesting Berlin had planted evidence in a deliberate provocation. “There is only one explanation offered: the need to counter an ‘aggressive Russia,’” Putin said. “But where is the proof? Well, now some ‘proof’ has been planted.” Putin’s remarks in Bishkek may have been bellicose, but he was a bit more conciliatory when it came to the Trump administration. Asked about the recent visit by CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow, Putin suggested Ratcliffe’s contacts with Russian intelligence officials were constructive, without letting slip any new details. “Contacts are always there, even during the most difficult times of the Cold War, and they are even more so now,” he said. “We favor negotiations, any negotiations, being filled first and foremost with concrete content. And if someone makes or can make a concrete contribution to this process, we’re all for it.” Putin also made clear whom he favors as interlocutors when it comes to striking any bargains with US President Donald Trump: the unconventional diplomatic duo of special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law. “These are people close to President Trump. In my opinion, they are sincere people and strive to bring concrete substance to our work. And the president trusts them, which is very important, and without this it is generally impossible to conduct any negotiations,” the Russian leader said. “Both Mr. Kushner and Witkoff are always welcome guests to us, and we are happy to work with them.” Witkoff and Kushner have made several trips to Moscow since Trump began his second term. But Putin’s preference may spark unease in Kyiv: Witkoff and Kushner have not visited Ukraine since taking on their roles as Trump’s point men for peace, and some observers worry they may support a deal weighted in Russia’s favor. Ukraine has a difficult winter ahead and there are fears Russia may launch a new wave of mobilization following parliamentary elections later this month. Putin said such speculation was “total BS.” But Putin’s comments about the animal kingdom may give a sense of where his head is these days. The orcas vs. polar bears story first surfaced during a meeting at Moscow Pedagogical State University on Saturday, when a participant mentioned a visit to the Arctic. That comment seemed to fire the imagination of the Russian president, who asked if the student had seen polar bears. “And killer whales live right next to them; they eat these bears like small fry – they attack in a pack and tear them apart,” Putin said, adding some political context: “That is the food chain, and children need to be told about this too, so they understand the world we live in and why we are conducting the Special Military Operation.” Several observers noted that orcas do not, in fact, hunt polar bears – and speculated whether Putin has been watching AI slop videos. But leaving aside the dubious zoology, Putin’s almost Trumpian non-sequitur suggested that, on the existential question of continuing war with Ukraine, his stance is as hard as ever. It’s always Shark Week in Putin’s world.

articles.title: America must focus on its strategic military priorities
articles.summary: U.S. Rep. Keith Self argues that the United States must prioritize reinforcing NATO and rebuilding its defense industrial capacity to deter Russian aggression in Europe rather than focusing solely on potential conflicts with China.
articles.body:
Current conflicts in Europe and the Middle East will end. When they do, military resources will be freed up for use around the globe. The U.S. must be laser focused on that day.

Throughout modern history, Russia has repeatedly demonstrated its readiness to achieve political aims through raw military force. Vladimir Putin’s Russia has relied on aggression as its default foreign policy tool. From Georgia in 2008 to Crimea in 2014 , and the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the lessons are clear: Russia’s intent is not defensive. It is imperial.

Russia’s drive to build a war-time economy, willingness to sustain high casualties and endure crippling economic sanctions underscores its determination. A regime that values ambition above human life presents a continual danger — especially to the fragile democracies of Eastern Europe.

The Baltic states, Poland, and even NATO itself are being tested. Strong counter moves require a commitment by our European partners to fill in gaps left by the Pentagon’s ill-advised reduction in force on the Eastern Frontier.

In China, the Chinese Communist Party governs with authoritarian zeal and has used economic coercion, cyber intrusion, and political influence to expand its footprint worldwide. But there is a crucial distinction between strategic hybrid war and immediate kinetic conflict.

For all its saber rattling about “reunification” with Taiwan, China has not initiated a major war in centuries. Its last significant military operation outside its borders was in 1979 — an effort that ended poorly . Chinese military writings emphasize deterrence, information dominance, and economic leverage far more than open warfare. The People’s Liberation Army has advanced weaponry and vast numbers, but it has not been tested in the crucible of war.

The notion that China will suddenly launch an amphibious invasion of Taiwan — one of the most complex military operations imaginable — defies historical precedent. Beijing’s leadership understands that such a move would unite the West, devastate its economy, and threaten the Communist Party’s grip on power.

The U.S. should continue to strengthen ties with Indo-Pacific allies, bolster deterrence, and safeguard freedom of navigation. But strategic prioritization requires more than preparing for hypothetical wars. It demands focusing our military readiness where violence is active and escalating.

For generations, Europe has been the anchor of Western democracy. Twice in the 20th century, American soldiers fought and died there to prevent tyranny from overrunning the continent. The peace and prosperity that followed were forged through American leadership and NATO solidarity.

Today, that legacy faces its toughest test since the Cold War. Europe needs to be strong. The U.S. projecting its commitment to European security sends a clear message to our adversaries that while keeping an eye turned towards the Indo-Pacific, our gaze is laser focused on the wolf that is closest to the sled.

Russia’s aggressive posture is designed to fracture NATO. Putin sees hesitation and debate in Western capitals as opportunities. Our task must therefore be the opposite — to show resolve, speed and strategic clarity. Reinforcing NATO’s eastern defenses and modernizing European command infrastructure are sound investments in deterrence.

Most weapons programs, and procurement priorities are currently centered on a future war with China that may never occur. Meanwhile, American and allied munitions stockpiles are being depleted in Europe and the Middle East, exposing critical gaps in our industrial base — from artillery shells to long-range missiles.

If the United States is to sustain global leadership, we must rebuild our defense industrial capacity around the threats we actually face. Strengthening our NATO partners does not weaken our Indo-Pacific posture; it enhances global deterrence by demonstrating that aggression will be resisted anywhere it occurs.

Moreover, the U.S. Army and Air Force require renewed investment. While the Navy’s Indo-Pacific presence remains essential, the defense of the European theater depends on land and air dominance, rapid logistics across interior lines, and intelligence coordination. Rebalancing our resources to ensure readiness in those domains is both prudent and necessary.

China observing a steadfast commitment to the defense of Western civilization is in itself deterrence. The stronger and more united NATO remains, the less incentive Beijing has to test us elsewhere. Indeed, defending Europe with resolve, indirectly influences peace in the Pacific.

Misdirecting American military could prove disastrous. Russia is redrawing borders through kinetic conflict. It is Russia’s aggression — not China’s ambition — currently testing the world’s resolve. Confronting that aggression decisively by sustaining our European Allies will help eliminate a strategic dilemma ahead of the problem at a smaller price — especially in American lives.

Keith Self represents the 3rd District of Texas and serves on the House Foreign Affairs and Veterans’ Affairs committees and as chairman of the Europe Subcommittee. He served in the U.S. Army for 25 years.

articles.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
articles.summary: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.
articles.body:
A woman, who was arrested for taking photos of jury members outside the courthouse in the Lindsay Clancy trial, has been charged with aggravated intimidation of a juror.

Dawn Light, 56, is accused of sitting in a restricted area outside the Plymouth courthouse and photographing jurors as they exited the building on Tuesday. Her lawyer called it a misunderstanding as she pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Lindsay Clancy, 36, is charged with the murders of her three children. The livestreamed trial has captured national and international media attention, and drawn strong, often deeply divided reactions from audiences.

The jury has been deliberating on the case since Thursday.

During Light's appearance in the court on Wednesday, Massachusetts lawyers said the sanctity of the judicial system was at risk because of her actions.

Light, a registered nurse with no prior criminal record, was ordered to stay away from the courthouse grounds and also from those associated with the Clancy trial. She was also ordered not to produce or disseminate photos that could have been preserved on iCloud.

Prosecutors requested a $50,000 (£37,000) cash bail, which was denied by the judge.

Jurors return in Lindsay Clancy trial after judge asks them to break deadlock

"This is a complete misunderstanding, Your Honour. My client was trying to get a picture of Ms Clancy," Light's attorney Jennifer White said in court.

After the arraignment, a swarm of reporters gathered around Light. When one asked, "Why did you want to see Lindsay [Clancy]", Light replied, "Why not?".

Authorities said they found Light in a restricted area in her parked car on Tuesday. When asked if she was taking videos, she said she was not and explained that she was waiting for Clancy.

Prosecutors alleged that when they went through Light's deleted folder on her phone, they found photos of jurors exiting the courthouse, and Light was then taken into custody.

Prosecutors said the courthouse has taken extensive measures to protect the trial that has created a spectacle in the coastal Massachusetts town. They described Light's conduct as a serious matter.

Judge William Sullivan, who is overseeing the Clancy trial, has an order specifically prohibiting the photographing or filming of jurors.

There are more than 200 reporters covering the case, and a group of women supporters - ebbing and flowing in size - have been coming to the courthouse over the past few weeks.

The case has also drawn wide attention on social media, stoking broader debates around mental health, postpartum psychosis, and the limits of criminal responsibility.

The Plymouth, Massachusetts, jury has been deliberating since Thursday over whether Clancy is criminally responsible for killing her children.

Despite the enormous media footprint, jurors deliberating the case are barred from watching or reading coverage of the trial. They are tasked with agreeing on a verdict solely on the evidence and testimony shown in court.

articles.title: Trump administration DOJ sues Kansas school district over transgender student guidelines and parental consent
articles.summary: In what it called “a first-of-its-kind lawsuit,” the Justice Department has sued a school district in Kansas over its guidelines on student gender identity and assisting transgender students.
articles.body: In what it called “a first-of-its-kind lawsuit,” the Justice Department has sued a school district in Kansas over its guidelines on student gender identity and assisting transgender students. The lawsuit, filed Monday, is the latest escalation from the Trump administration targeting school districts for policies or guidelines to accommodate transgender students in academic settings. The Justice Department said it was seeking to stop the Kansas City, Kansas, public school district from violating federal law by “facilitating secret ‘gender transitions’ for children at school without their parents’ knowledge or consent.” “Parental rights are paramount in the operation of America’s public schools, and Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools does not know children better than their own parents,” Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, said in a statement. “The Department will not tolerate school districts playing fast and loose with federal law in the service of radical gender ideology.” The complaint says district guidelines violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), which allow parents to view students’ educational records and threaten loss of federal funding for failing to comply. The district is at risk of losing nearly $70 million in federal funding if it is found teachers or administrators withheld information related to a student’s gender identity, NBC News affiliate KSHB 41 reports. According to the Justice Department complaint, the Kansas City district’s guidance says that a student or their parents should contact the school if a student is transgender or gender nonconforming and is seeking any related accommodations. “If any staff member learns a student is transgender or gender non-conforming, that information should be relayed to the school principal without delay,” the guideline says, according to the complaint. “The school principal should discuss available accommodations and resources with the student or the student’s parent or legal guardian, including the availability of a planning meeting. If it becomes known that the student does not want the student’s parent or legal guardian included at this stage, that request will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.” The guidelines say those requests will be evaluated by the executive director of Student Services & Family Support, the director of Student Support Programs, the executive director of Equity and Inclusion and the district’s attorney. “When reviewing the request, the district will consider the student’s age, the student’s grade level, the student’s welfare based on the information available to the district at that time, and any other relevant information,” the guidelines say, according to the complaint. The school district’s guidance also says that upon request, administrators will schedule a planning meeting to discuss a student’s preferred pronoun use and restroom and locker use. The district for 21,000 students said in a statement to KSHB this week that it’s been in full cooperation with federal law and is “disappointed by the DOJ’s decision to file the lawsuit.” Because the matter is now pending in federal court, district leaders said they would respond to the complaint through the appropriate legal channel and not issue additional public comments. After the Justice Department threatened to sue the district in late July, KCKPS Superintendent Anna ‌Stubblefield told KSHB 41 that she could not recall an incident in which the district withheld such information from parents. “It also is not policy, it is guidance,” Stubblefield said. “There’s nowhere in the guidance where we say ‘withhold information from parents.’ We have no reason or incentive to withhold information from parents about anything that they’re entitled to for their students.” The lawsuit comes after the Justice Department in April said it determined that four school districts in Kansas were in violation of the Family Education Rights and Privacy Act. The Trump administration has previously threatened to cut federal funding from school districts over policies regarding transgender students and gender identity, including in Maryland and Michigan. In March, the Supreme Court barred California from enforcing state rules that restrict when schools can notify parents about students who come out as transgender and require teachers to use children’s preferred pronouns. Lawyers for the state had argued that the policies were not as broad as the plaintiffs suggested. “Currently, under California’s laws and constitutional provisions on privacy and antidiscrimination, schools may balance parental interests with students’ particular needs and circumstances, such as the risk of harm upon disclosure of the student’s gender identity without student consent,” they wrote at the time. The rules “allow disclosure to parents in some circumstances and limit disclosure in others,” the lawyers said.

articles.title: Princess Diana's godson Prince Philippos and Princess Nina welcome first child, son Kimon Thomas Konstantinos, via surrogate in the US nearly six years after their wedding
articles.summary: UK News: Prince Philippos and Princess Nina of Greece have become parents for the first time, welcoming a baby boy via surrogate earlier this summer in the Uni.
articles.body: Prince Philippos and Princess Nina of Greece have become parents for the first time, welcoming a baby boy via surrogate earlier this summer in the United States. The former Greek royal family announced the arrival on September 1, revealing that their son, Kimon Thomas Konstantinos, was born on July 27, 2026. The couple had not previously disclosed that they were expecting a child.According to Hello Magazine, a statement from the office of the former Royal Family of Greece said Philippos and Nina were announcing “with great joy” the birth of their first child and expressed their gratitude to the surrogate mother, her family and the medical professionals who supported them throughout the journey.“Philip and Nina are enjoying these first precious weeks together with Kimonas and are deeply happy to begin, together with their son, this new chapter in their family's life,” the statement added.Son's name pays tribute to both familiesThe baby's middle names carry special significance for the couple. “Thomas” honours Nina's father, Swiss businessman and VistaJet founder Thomas Flohr, while “Konstantinos” is believed to pay tribute to Philippos' late father, Constantine II, the last King of Greece, who died in 2023.No photographs of the newborn have been shared publicly so far.Philippos, 40, is the youngest child of Constantine II and Queen Anne-Marie of Denmark. He was born in London and raised there before moving to the United States, where he has worked as a financial analyst.Nina, 39, is the daughter of billionaire businessman Thomas Flohr and is known for founding Kisawa Sanctuary and her work in conservation and hospitality.Couple's three weddings before becoming parentsThe birth comes less than four months before Philippos and Nina's sixth wedding anniversary.The couple first married in a private civil ceremony in St. Moritz, Switzerland, in December 2020. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, only their fathers attended as witnesses.Nina later shared a photograph from the ceremony on Instagram with the caption, “Just married (civilly).”They subsequently held a second, low-key celebration in Cambridgeshire in May 2021 before exchanging vows for a third time in a lavish religious ceremony at the Metropolitan Cathedral of Athens in October 2021.For the Athens wedding, Nina wore a Chanel gown and the Antique Corsage Tiara that had belonged to her mother-in-law, Queen Anne-Marie.The ceremony was attended by several prominent members of European royalty and society, including Princess Beatrice and Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi, Princess Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank, and members of the Greek and Danish royal families.Philippos is one of Princess Diana's godchildrenPhilippos has strong connections to the British royal family. He was one of the godchildren of the late Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, and his late father, Constantine II, was a close friend of King Charles and the godfather of Prince William.Philippos was born in 1986 at St Mary's Hospital in London and grew up in a 13-bedroom home near Hampstead Heath. Princess Diana was reportedly a frequent visitor to the property with her sons, Prince William and Prince Harry.Despite his royal connections, Philippos has generally maintained a private life and has built a career in finance in New York.Former Greek royals regained citizenship in 2024Philippos' new status as a father comes after an important development for the former Greek royal family.In 2024, Philippos and other members of his family had their Greek citizenship reinstated after being stripped of it in 1994 during a long-running dispute over former royal property and the family's relationship with the Greek state.Following the restoration of their nationality, members of the family adopted the surname “De Grece”, meaning “of Greece” in French.The family's Greek citizenship had been revoked decades after the monarchy was abolished in a 1974 referendum. Constantine II and his family subsequently lived in exile for years, with the former king eventually returning to Greece as a private citizen.The citizenship restoration applied to 10 members of the former royal family, including Constantine II and Anne-Marie's five children and five grandchildren.A growing European royal family connectionPhilippos' siblings include Crown Prince Pavlos, Prince Nikolaos and Princesses Alexia and Theodora. Pavlos and his wife, Marie-Chantal, have five children, including Odysseas-Kimon, who shares part of the name now given to Philippos' newborn son.Philippos' extended family also includes Queen Sofia of Spain, his paternal aunt and the mother of Spain's King Felipe VI, as well as members of the Danish royal family through his mother, Queen Anne-Marie.With the arrival of Kimon Thomas Konstantinos, Philippos and Nina now begin a new chapter as parents, nearly six years after their first wedding.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan: Imran Khan's sister files fresh contempt plea over denied jail visits
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan's sister Uzma Khan on Wednesday filed a fresh contempt of court petition in the Supreme Court, alleging non-.
articles.body: Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan's sister Uzma Khan on Wednesday filed a fresh contempt of court petition in the Supreme Court, alleging non-enforcement of previous judicial directives issued by the country's apex court.In her petition, Uzma named several high-ranking officials, including Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif and Adiala (Rawalpindi Central Jail) Superintendent Sajid Baig, as respondents.According to the Express Tribune, the petition was filed after the Supreme Court's August 18 instructions, which mandated virtual communication between Imran Khan and his sons, alongside weekly access for his sisters, failed to materialise.The plea said that Uzma Khan was denied a scheduled visit on Tuesday and noted that audio communication with his sons has remained restricted since March.The petition alleged that authorities neglected to establish the necessary infrastructure enabling bi-weekly telephone calls with his sons, Kasim Khan and Sulaiman Khan, as previously ordered by the bench.Earlier, Uzma had filed another contempt application addressing government non-compliance regarding a separate instruction within the August 18 order, which directed that Imran Khan be moved to Shifa International Hospital for medical care.Under the original August 18 decision, the Supreme Court instructed that the former premier be transferred to Shifa International Hospital for clinical evaluation by a multidisciplinary medical panel while simultaneously granting visitation rights.Following the orders, authorities transferred Imran Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) on August 21. He was, however, sent back to Adiala Jail shortly after medical personnel declared him to be "medically fit".Reacting to the developments, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) lambasted prison administrators for barring relatives from seeing the party founder, characterising the restrictions as a flagrant breach of mandates issued by both the Supreme Court and the Islamabad High Court, as reported by another Pakistan-based daily, Dawn.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: South African airline Airlink behind daring stadium stunt cancels next flyby, regulator says
articles.summary: The civil aviation authority says it is also investigating last Saturday's aerial display.
articles.body:
The South African airline behind a daring aerial stunt last Saturday that saw two planes flying in close formation low over a packed stadium has pulled out of doing a similar operation this weekend, the country's aviation regulator, SACAA, has said.

Airlink's flying feat divided opinion with some labelling the startling manoeuvre reckless, while others praised the precision and expertise on display.

SACAA said that while it had approved the applications and safety measures for the flybys, it was now investigating further following "discussions in the media".

Airlink has not commented on the reported cancellation of Saturday's display that had been due to place over a stadium in Soweto.

Footage of last weekend's air show before the start of a rugby match in Cape Town, featuring fierce rivals South Africa and New Zealand, was shared around the world.

The flight tracking website Flightradar24 said that according to its analysis "the lead aircraft passed less than 50ft (15m) above the top of the stadium".

From some angles the jets appeared very close to the roof of the DHL Stadium as they roared over amid coloured flare smoke.

The airline said the flights were performed with the "approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the flypast" and were conducted by a "highly experienced crew".

But Airlink will not be repeating the flights over the stadium in Soweto, Johannesburg, that is hosting the third and deciding test between the Springboks and the All Blacks, according to SACAA.

The regulator said that while the company had followed all the correct procedures it had now "obtained the flight data recording downloads as well as other additional requirements" for further analysis.

"SACAA, as the safety net of the South African skies, gives the public the assurance that aviation safety and security compliance will always remain paramount and is not negotiable," it said in a statement emphasising the excellent air safety record in the country.

The flyby has been a feature at major sporting and presidential events in South Africa several times over the years - using both military jets and commercial airlines.

articles.title: Look of the Week: Nicole Kidman, in witchy splendor, hints at Versace’s next chapter
articles.summary: Nicole Kidman’s lacy Versace gown for “Practical Magic 2” may be spellbinding, but Pieter Mulier, the new creative director behind the look, has his own spell to cast, too.
articles.body: For the past week, Nicole Kidman, Sandra Bullock, Maisie Williams and Joey King have ushered in the season of the witch as their coven has assembled for the “Practical Magic 2” press tour. Each have had their standout looks, from King’s sheer Miu Miu florals to Williams’ crimson throwback ode to Bullock, but the asymmetrical drop-waist lacy gown Kidman wore to the Los Angeles premiere on Monday teased more than just the film. The enchanting look was fitting for a free-spirited witch lounging around her candlelit home sanctuary, as Kidman’s character Gillian might do. (Fans will also be happy to hear the “Practical Magic” house, which has gained its own cult following, was reportedly rebuilt for the sequel). Completed with a wide lace choker and tousled hair, the romantic dress was also the first glimpse into Versace’s next chapter. Since taking the creative helm in February, designer Pieter Mulier has not yet had the opportunity to send a collection down the runway — and he won’t until early next year, skipping the Spring-Summer 2027 shows next month. Dressing Kidman is the only hint, for now, of how he’ll steer the famed Italian luxury house since Dario Vitale’s divisive 1980s-saturated one-and-done collection. Kidman’s red carpet look teases what we might see from Mulier’s much-anticipated debut collection for the Italian luxury house. The timing of this sneak peek is also interesting: To make that big of a statement during the premiere of “Practical Magic 2” shows just how far the cult-classic film has come since its poor critical reviews and fast box-office drop-off. “We thought, ‘This is going to be such an amazing film. People are going to love it,’” Bullock told Variety at the sequel’s premiere. “And then it got quiet.” The original premiere wasn’t a headlining moment, either, though it was well attended by the likes of Heath Ledger, LeeAnn Rimes and Matthew McConaughey. Premieres back then were much more casual affairs, not vehicles for major fashion moments. Because she was onstage in London at the time, Kidman didn’t even attend, leaving Bullock to promote it with her other castmates. And when, earlier in the week, Williams paid tribute to Bullock with a throwback look, it wasn’t to the little black dress from the 1998 premiere, but instead, an all-red look the actor wore the following year for a different film, “Forces of Nature.” The fact that “Practical Magic” got a sequel at all is a testament to the brewing nostalgia built over three decades. Kidman and Bullock’s sisterly chemistry, the nearly all-female cast, the camp value, and the film’s lore trickling out over the years have also contributed to a recent resurgence of interest. And despite the fact that “Practical Magic” was never a fashion film, it has become a kind of holy grail for witchy aura and autumnal mood boards, the kind of feeling you hope to have by wearing a slip dress or slouchy cardigan, listening to Stevie Nicks during the hour of the wolf — in your beautiful, botanical-filled, Roman & Williams designed house. That’s a mood that Versace seems to be happy to capitalize on. It’s a blueprint the luxury house and others have followed before by trickling out a new designer’s vision ahead of the official debut. Vitale’s collection was preempted with a blazer and jeans combo worn by both Julia Roberts and Amanda Seyfied that went viral, and Ayo Edebiri also generated buzz when she test-drove Mathieu Blazy’s first Chanel looks in Venice last year. That Mulier would want to tap into the type of divine feminine energy that “Practical Magic 2” is offering makes sense, in the hopes that his version of Versace will likewise cast an early spell.

articles.title: Rescuers use ziplines to transport trapped citizens after devastating Nepal floods decimate country's bridges
articles.summary: Video shows rescue workers using cable cars and ziplines to ferry stranded citizens across flooded rivers in Nepal after the deadly mudslide.
articles.body: Rescue workers in Nepal were forced to use cable cars and ziplines to ferry stranded citizens across rivers after August's deadly flood and mudslide wiped out local bridges. Video shows teams of workers yanking ropes to ferry locals who were stranded on an embankment flanked by a flooded river. In one clip, a pair of people sit in a small box attached to a wire as they're yanked onto a platform across a river in Nuwakot, Nepal. The rescues come as both Nepal and neighboring China continue to deal with the aftermath of the Aug. 26 mudslide and ensuing floods in Tibet's Gyirong Valley and the Nepal's Trishuli River Valley. EXPERTS ZERO IN ON LIKELY CAUSE OF DEADLY NEPAL MUDSLIDE, WITH MORE THAN 1,400 MISSING As of Wednesday, at least 1,114 people have been confirmed dead and nearly 4,000 remain missing in Nepal. Chinese authorities report an additional 16 confirmed dead and at least 541 missing on their side of the border. Rescuers are still working to search and rescue any potential survivors trapped in a hydropower tunnel in the Rasuwa district. ROUGHLY 80 AMERICANS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR AFTER HIMALAYAN DISASTER KILLS 903, OFFICIALS SAY "In Rasuwagadhi, we think 46 people are trapped in a room-like structure in the tunnel," Amshu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal Electricity Authority that operates the hydropower plant, told Reuters. A senior official in President Donald Trump's administration also told Fox News that an additional two Americans made it to safety in Nepal, marking 16 total Americans in the country who made their way to safety. SON REALIZES MISSING AMERICAN DAD WAS IN PATH OF NEPAL DISASTER AFTER WATCHING VIRAL VIDEO Seventy-five Americans in Nepal currently remain unaccounted for while no American casualties have been reported so far.
