articles.title: China's Xi Jinping tells Middle East to be ‘masters of their own destiny’ amid Iran war
articles.summary: China News: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Middle Eastern countries to oppose external interference and consider reshaping the region's security order dur.
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Middle Eastern countries to oppose external interference and consider reshaping the region's security order during talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday, as Beijing seeks to expand its influence amid the US war against Iran.Xi, on his first visit to the Middle East in four years, said countries in the region should be “masters of their own destiny” and explore a new regional “security architecture”, according to China's state news agency Xinhua.The Chinese leader also said Beijing was ready to work with countries in the region to safeguard shipping routes, an issue that has gained greater significance after the conflict disrupted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb.Egypt and China expand security, economic cooperationXi was welcomed by Sisi with a military ceremony in Cairo. The two leaders agreed to deepen security cooperation and counterterrorism coordination.According to a joint statement, the two sides also agreed to expand cooperation in data centres, semiconductors and critical metals supply chains, while strengthening the use of their currencies in trade and investment.In talks with Sisi, Xi also said the two countries should jointly oppose what he described as “unilateralism and acts of bullying”, Xinhua reported, according to AP. He called for efforts towards “a more just and equitable global governance system”.Egypt, a major US defence partner that receives around $1.3 billion annually in military aid from Washington, has been steadily increasing economic and military cooperation with China in recent years.For Cairo, closer ties with Beijing form part of a broader policy of diversifying its international partnerships. In an article published ahead of Xi's visit, Sisi said Egypt was pursuing a policy of “strategic balance” at a time of increasing global rivalry.“Egypt wants to widen the circle of its relations with major world powers, including China,” former Egyptian diplomat Ayman Zaineldine told Reuters. “So the visions converge.”China sees Egypt as key regional partnerFor Beijing, Egypt's regional influence, strategic location, large domestic market and connections with Africa make it an important partner as China seeks to expand its economic and diplomatic role in the region.“Egypt represents something quite valuable to Beijing – a large domestic market for investment opportunities, and a lot of diplomatic weight in the region, including the Palestine question, as well as connectivity to Africa,” H A Hellyer, a scholar at the Royal United Services Institute think tank, told Reuters.Xi's visit comes at a time when China is seeking to cultivate deeper ties with one of Washington's key allies in the Middle East while presenting itself as a stabilising force in the region.Xi's trip to Egypt is his first to the country in a decade and his first visit to the Middle East since travelling to Saudi Arabia in 2022.Growing military ties between Cairo and Beijing were also on display last month during Egypt's “Eagles of Civilisation” exercises with China, which included a rare air combat drill involving Chinese-made J-16 jets and French-made Rafale aircraft.Chinese investment and trade continue to growHome to the Suez Canal and with a population of more than 110 million, Egypt is an important market for China. Egypt imported about $10 billion worth of Chinese goods in the first half of this year.Chinese investment in Egypt has grown significantly since Sisi visited China and signed a strategic partnership agreement in 2014. Chinese companies have invested in container ports, green hydrogen projects and facilities producing iron pipes, car tyres and satellites.Egypt's cabinet has said the Suez Canal Economic Zone has attracted around $4 billion in Chinese investment. On Wednesday, Egyptian authorities announced plans to expand a Chinese-developed industrial area in the zone, while ZC Rubber Group signed a preliminary agreement to study a $500 million tyre manufacturing complex.China has invested more than $10 billion in Egypt, while annual trade between the two countries is estimated at $20 billion, based on government figures.The Suez Canal has also gained greater importance as an alternative route for energy supplies amid heavy disruption to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.“China has good reason to strengthen ties with the country that controls the route still open,” said Muhammad Zulfikar Rakhmat, a Middle East expert with Jakarta's Centre of Economic and Law Studies, as cited by news agency AP.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. The activists, who were previously detained by Israeli authorities, have been held in Tunis’s Mornaguia Prison for over five months, sparking concerns about their well-being and prompting a hunger strike by one of the detainees.

The Tunisian government's actions have been criticized by international activists, who argue that solidarity with Gaza should not be criminalized, and have called for the release of the detained activists.

A Brazilian activist has demanded the release of four Tunisian colleagues who were part of the Global Sumud Flotilla that attempted to break the Israeli blockade on Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid last year.

Activists from multiple countries around the world boarded dozens of boats, launching the flotilla in August 2025, to carry life-saving supplies to Gaza. They were subsequently intercepted by Israel, with those on board detained.

Israeli authorities released Nabil Channoufi, Ghassan Henchiri, Ghassan Boughdiri, and Wael Naouar from prison and they returned to Tunisia in October. Fellow activists said Tunisian "counterterrorism" police rearrested the four in February, after they announced a new flotilla mission to carry aid to Gaza.

"It's been so long, my dear friends," said Brazilian activist Thiago Avila, in a video message posted on social media on Tuesday.

"I'm writing to you this letter after 170 days since you've been arrested while mobilising solidarity with Palestine through our peaceful mission of the Global Sumud Flotilla to break the illegal siege of Gaza," he said.

In March, the United Kingdom-based news site the Morning Star reported that the activists were detained by the Tunisian National Guard financial crimes unit for alleged money laundering, fraud and misuse of funds collected through flotilla campaign donations.

They have been held in Tunis's Mornaguia Prison for more than five months, according to family members and fellow activists. Tunisia's government has not publicly commented on the situation.

"No one should be detained and separated from their families for acting in solidarity with a people victim of a genocide," Avila said.

"No one, especially in Tunisia, where the people are connected with Palestine with all their hearts and [where they] supported our mission even in the hardest circumstances."

Avila said that a hunger strike by Wael Naouar has stretched on for at least seven days. The activist added he and Naouar had taken a similar action while held in Israeli detention last year.

"You've been fainting, throwing up blood, and with a critical medical condition," he said.

Israel imposed an air, land and sea blockade on Gaza to prevent food, water, medicine and other supplies from entering the enclave since 2007, when Hamas took control of Gaza. That blockade was intensified in October 2023 amid Israel's genocidal war that followed Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.

The Freedom Flotilla Coalition is an international network of organisations that has launched multiple missions to Gaza since 2010, including the Sumud Flotilla, to deliver humanitarian aid.

Beyond last year's Sumud mission, organisers also launched a flotilla this year that was intercepted by Israeli forces in April.

Activists have accused Tunisia's government of seeking to stop the flotillas, which have regularly used the Sidi Bou Said port in the country's north to organise.

Beyond the arrests, activists have accused the government of banning gatherings and other events related to the flotillas.

articles.title: California condo owners were suddenly handed a $26,000 HOA bill each; an 81-year-old resident says she may have to leave the home she worked hard to keep
articles.summary: US News: Residents of the Vilamoura condominium complex in San Clemente, California, are facing sudden financial pressure after their homeowners association is.
articles.body: Residents of the Vilamoura condominium complex in San Clemente, California, are facing sudden financial pressure after their homeowners association issued a mandatory emergency assessment of more than $26,000 per unit to pay for complete roof replacements. The unexpected charge affects all 198 units in the South Orange County complex and has led to strong opposition from homeowners, especially retirees living on fixed incomes. By declaring the roof work an emergency, the homeowners association board avoided the normal community voting process required for major capital projects.Beverly Albright, an 81-year-old resident who has lived at the complex for years, said she was deeply upset by the sudden bill in an interview with local television station ABC7 Eyewitness News. "I will have to move. And this was my... I've worked very hard to make it so that I could be here," Albright told the broadcast station. According to ABC7 Eyewitness News and regional news site Patch, the homeowners association gave residents three ways to pay. They can pay the full $26,000 upfront, make two large payments, or use an instalment plan requiring more than $2,000 per month for six months, followed by $400 each month.Residents challenge emergency status and board authorityHomeowners who oppose the charge say the roof replacement does not qualify as a real emergency. Some residents claim the board allowed the roofs to deteriorate for years and is now calling the long-delayed maintenance an emergency to avoid getting approval from the community. Under California law, homeowners association boards can impose special assessments without a vote only in limited emergency situations. These can include immediate threats to a building’s structure or repairs ordered by a court. Vilamoura residents argue that the roofs do not show active failure or an immediate risk of collapse that would justify skipping the normal voting process. Residents are also questioning whether the board received enough competitive bids from roofing contractors to make sure the project is fairly priced. An attorney who handles homeowners association matters told ABC7 Eyewitness News that state law generally requires homeowners to pay disputed assessments while legal challenges continue. Failure to pay could lead to property liens or even foreclosure proceedings by the board. The Vilamoura homeowners association board declined to comment publicly on the assessment. It cited ongoing legal consultations and privacy concerns related to property management.Legal action and recall efforts gain momentumIn response to the large assessment, affected homeowners have organised a campaign to challenge the decision through legal and administrative channels. According to Patch and local community updates, residents have started a formal recall effort to remove current members of the homeowners association board. They are also seeking an immediate injunction to stop collection of the assessment while an independent review of the association’s reserve funds and the condition of the roofs is carried out. To help neighbours facing serious financial pressure or the possibility of losing their homes, community members have also created a GoFundMe campaign. The fundraiser aims to pay for legal representation and provide emergency financial help to elderly residents such as Albright.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: An American CEO, Hany Girgis, who is known on X for his anti-H-1B social media posts, shared some screenshots that he claimed to have received from a VP at a Fortune 500 company exposing H-1B abuse. The post went viral at a time when the H-1B visa program had emerged as the most controversial issue, as the Donald Trump administration is taking several steps to end abuse in the program, but which will also make legal immigration for jobs difficult in the US.The purported screenshots exposed multi-layer abuses that start with the hiring process. When an H-1B employee is involved in the process, only certain preferred candidates are selected and Americans are rejected. Even before the interview, sometimes the interview questions are shared and some kickbacks may also be involved in the process. This means that if a certain candidate is hired, a vendor/IT staffing company may give some benefits or kickbacks.In the second stage, these preferred employees are given high-profile assignments and more visibility while American workers are given "unusually aggressive deadlines", the screenshot claimed.Another major allegation was raised in the post, alluding to a second type of syndicate. "There are lots of Indian grocery stores and restaurants which came up in TX, especially Dallas and Austin. Manager and their subordinates are partners. All take turns so that one is at a grocery store or restaurant always. This is another source of income for them," it added.As the post went viral, America First activists started India-bashing. Florida Republican Chandler Langevin narrowed down the allegations and said H-1B just means Indian. "Let’s stop tiptoeing through the tulips here. There wouldn’t be a problem with the H-1b program if we were bringing over Germans and Japanese. The problem is Indians. It doesn’t matter if they have an H-1b, an OPT, or a green card… Indian scamming culture and Indian nationalism is not compatible with American culture and business practices. Stop being afraid of being called names and say what the problem is. INDIANS," Langevin wrote.Some social media users, however, questioned the veracity of the claims and asked why the VP at a Fortune 500 company could not take action if there was any abuse.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Gunman in deadly Swiss rave attack ‘lone perpetrator’, police say
articles.summary: Police say no indication anyone else involved in attack that killed 22-year-old Italian woman.
articles.body:
The man suspected of fatally shooting an Italian woman at a rave in Switzerland’s Aarau was a “lone perpetrator”, according to police.

The commander ⁠of the Aargau cantonal police, Michael Leupold, said at a news conference on Wednesday that there was no indication anyone else had been involved in the attack early on Sunday that killed a 22-year-old Italian woman and wounded five people.

“We, therefore, ‌assume with a high degree of certainty that the shooting was the act of one individual,” Leupold said.

The suspect, a 43-year-old Swiss man, handed himself in on Monday to police in Delemont in northwestern Switzerland’s Jura canton and has remained silent while in custody, according to prosecutors.

Leupold said the motive for the attack was not known and the suspect was not previously known to police.

The suspected gunman suffers from “psychological problems” and has maintained his silence since his arrest, Aargau cantonal prosecutor Christoph Ruedi said.

The attack has been met with public shock in Switzerland, where shootings, particularly those involving several victims, are rare despite widespread gun ownership.

Authorities said two pistols and an AK-47 assault rifle were found in the suspect’s car.

The rave’s organisers, meanwhile, said they were “shocked and devastated”, writing on their website that they “will do everything in our power to support the police in their work”.

“A rave should always be a place of joy and love. Never a place where people are killed, injured or left in fear.”

articles.title: Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron join King Charles and Queen Camilla in private viewing of famed Bayeux Tapestry
articles.summary: Britain’s King Charles III and Queen Camilla were joined by the French president and first lady at the British Museum in London on Wednesday for a private tour of the Bayeux Tapestry — a world-famous artwork depicting a fateful battle between the two nations.
articles.body: Britain’s King Charles III and Queen Camilla were joined by the French president and first lady at the British Museum in London on Wednesday for a private tour of the Bayeux Tapestry — a world-famous artwork depicting a fateful battle between the two nations. Emmanuel and Brigitte Macron are on a two-day visit to the United Kingdom, in a bid to foster closer ties between the two European countries. Their trip began with a visit to see the 11th-century embroidery — currently on loan to Britain from France — which arrived in the UK in July after an absence of more than 900 years. Also joining the two couples on the tour of the blockbuster exhibition, which opens to the public next week, were the recently appointed British prime minister, Andy Burnham, and his wife, Marie-France van Heel. In the role since July 20, it is the first time that Burnham has met the French leader. Stretching to 70 meters long (230 feet), the Bayeux Tapestry is not actually a tapestry at all but an embroidery of dyed wool stitched onto a bleached linen background. Created 960 years ago, it depicts the events leading up to the Battle of Hastings in 1066, which saw William of Normandy seize the throne from Harold Godwinson, the last Anglo-Saxon king of England. The loan of the work to the British Museum follows a historic agreement reached between the two countries after years of negotiation, and exhaustive planning to transport it safely from its permanent home in Normandy, northern France. “The return of the Bayeux Tapestry to England is a landmark moment in the history of our two nations, and I want people everywhere in the country to be able to enjoy it,” Burnham said in a statement, according to PA Media. Tickets for the first stage of the exhibition sold out as soon as they went on sale earlier this year, with the British Museum recording its single biggest day of ticket sales in its history — more than £2.4 million ($3.2 million) in sales in the first 24 hours. The VIPs were met at the museum by its director, Nicholas Cullinan, and George Osborne, a former British finance minister who is now the museum’s chair. They were then led along the length of the tapestry, as curators pointed out the key moments depicted within it. After the tour, the dignitaries gathered in the museum’s glass-topped Great Court.

articles.title: Putin and Iran 'need each other desperately,' expert says, as Russia voices support for regime
articles.summary: Vladimir Putin declared full solidarity with Iran as an expert said both nations "need each other desperately" during the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict.
articles.body: The relationship between Iran and Russia is growing as both sides "need each other desperately," an expert told Fox News Digital on Wednesday after Russian President Vladimir Putin voiced support for the regime in Tehran. Putin was photographed shaking hands Tuesday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during a meeting on the sidelines on the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit in Kyrgyzstan, where he said, "Russia is standing in full solidarity with the people of Iran," according to a readout by the Kremlin. "We admire your courage and resilience in your fight for your national interests," Putin added. "Please convey my regards and words of sincere support to Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei." U.S. Air Force retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, a former NATO commander, told Fox News Digital that "this relationship between Iran and Russia is growing" and "they both need each other desperately." "In the grand scheme of things, they are both 'broke.' I'm using others language here, but the bottom line is they are hurting economically," he said. "They need each other's help. Russia desperately needs Iran to produce missiles for them because of Ukraine's attack on Russia's ability to build missiles. And Iran desperately needs Russian targeting and intelligence to continue to attack Americans in the Middle East." RUSSIA'S LAVROV SAYS IRAN HAS 'INALIENABLE' RIGHT TO ENRICH URANIUM, OPENLY DEFYING TRUMP'S DEMANDS "Russia is transferring capability, transferring, in larger terms, technologies that enable Iran, and frankly, they're sort of helping to prop up the religious leaders of Iran," Breedlove added. Jason Brodsky, the policy director of United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), told Fox News Digital that "Iran and Russia have had a long-time partnership that is strategically important for both countries." "Russia views Iran as a cudgel to use against America, and Iran has in recent years especially viewed Russia as a lifeline with respect to advancing its military, providing economic support, providing political support, most importantly at the U.N. Security Council as Russia is a permanent member. So that's how the partnership serves both countries' interests," he said. Breedlove also said the U.S. war with Iran has now "turned into almost more a test of will than it is a military test." Both the U.S. military and Iran have been trading aerial strikes in recent days. "The U.S. has established basically air and sea dominance, but because of the U.S.' decision early in the war that they were not going to put boots on the ground, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps knows that they're going to survive. And Iran's IRGC, in their mind, understand clearly that they don't have to win this war," Breedlove told Fox News Digital. "All they have to do is survive and continue to threaten" the Strait of Hormuz, which will drive up maritime insurance rates and cause "all kinds of problems with carriers," he continued. "So we have a test of wills, a nation that can militarily end the war, should it make some more drastic decisions about how to get after the IRGC and a nation that understands it doesn't have to win, it just has to survive, because its harassment of the strait will cause prices to go so high on transit that it's going to be a problem for the world economy," Breedlove said. CHINA, RUSSIA, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA FORM 'AXIS OF AGGRESSORS' THAT COULD OVERWHELM US, BOOK WARNS Brodsky told Fox News Digital that he believes there is "no diplomatic happy ending" for the U.S.-Iran war "as long as the Iranian regime is in power." "It is fundamentally anti-American to its core and that imperils any kind of diplomatic arrangement or negotiating process that the United States and Iran undertake," he said. "I think we've seen in President Trump's comments that he has grown exasperated with diplomacy with the Islamic Republic, and rightfully so." During their meeting Tuesday, Pezeshkian told Putin, "We are grateful to you for the stance you have adopted during the war, the conflicts, the U.S. sanctions and all the rest," according to the Kremlin. "Our relations are of a strategic nature. This is more than just ‘normal’ relations," Pezeshkian reportedly added. "We believe – no, we are certain that thanks to this we can stand up against U.S. bias and the rightless sanctions they are imposing on us." VIDEO: US LAUNCHES STRIKES ON IRAN AS TRUMP WARNS REGIME IS 'PLAYING OUT THE INEVITABLE' Breedlove said to Fox News Digital following the Putin-Pezeshkian meeting that "the world has a problem with Russia, and for almost 25 or 30 years we tried to make a friend or at least a cooperative entity out of Russia." "We wanted to embrace them and bring them into the Western fold and so forth. And now we are clearly understanding based on what they're doing for Iran and what they are doing in their illegal and immoral war in Ukraine, we now understand that Russia does not want to be a part of the Western world," he said. "Mr. Putin has this vision of three spheres of influence. Mr. Xi [of China] takes care of Eastern Asia. Russia takes care of Western Asia and Europe, and the United States should remain in the Western Hemisphere. And that's what he's pushing us to," Breedlove continued. "And the bottom line is, in respect to Iran and in respect to Ukraine, Mr. Putin is going to do nothing until someone shows him steel. He understands power. Rhetoric doesn't do anything with Mr. Putin."
